Alright. So after 14 hours of gameplay in the first 24 hours of the game being out and almost 100% completion, (I think I'm at 96% or something) I can safely say that this is a
good game. The island kingdom of Gemea is a joy to explore, filled with resources, collectibles, and unlockables. The towns and settlements that dot the landscape all feel unique and interesting (especially mountain town, which I won't spoil because I believe that it should be experienced firsthand). The world is pretty decently sized ( I feel like it is about half the size of Skyrim's map, so not too shabby). There is a fast-travel point in each biome, which works out most of the time, except in the desert biome where the fast travel point seems a bit too out of the way in relation to the key areas in the biome. There are also a few single-use-a-day teleportation points on the map that open up at specific times in the day.
Touching on the story, it's not really a major part of the game, nor is it very exstensive. This wasn't necessarily a bad thing since I spent most of my time exploring the world or completing side quests, which made the main quest feel longer than it truly was. Completing the main quest does however allow you to become a "master craftsman" which gives you access to some very helpful items, aswell as some pretty nice customization options.
Character customization in this game is very reminiscent of Animal Crossing, where you start off with a character that has little customization options. In this game you choose your body type, hair color, and eye color. Later on, you can either craft or trade for other customization options, such as hair styles, hair colors, outfits, facial hair, backpacks, and badges (which show on your backpack of choice). Exploring different combinations was fun and I eventually found an outfit that I liked.
Farming starts out with animals only, which you bribe with their favorite foods to lure them back to your farm(s) to adopt them. Later on, once you become a master carpenter or constructer (constructor? constructioner? construction worker?) you have the ability to craft tree planters and garden patches which allow you to grow crops. (PRO TIP: If you postion a large animal coop against the roof of the grasslands farmhouse with the tallest part touching the farmhouse roof and place water or food trough at the lower part of the coop you can hop up on the farmhouse roof and get a tree planter early on. Hope you could figure out what I was trying to say there.)
Fishing is different that most other fishing minigames I've played, although I'm not sure if you can fail catching a fish. I haven't tested it nor had a line break while catching fish. Not really much else to say on that topic.
Now for the gripes. The things I was disappointed in. Cons. There's not a lot of these and they by no means ruin the game for me but they made me a little upset when I figured them out.
I think that's about it. The developers said they were planning some updates that could add player housing which would add a nice new layer to the game that I think could make it a lot better than it is now, which is impressive because this is already a magnificent game. If you like exploration-y collect-athons with loveable characters, immersive landscapes, and a pretty decent soundtrack that you can chill out to, I
recommend this game!

Ambitious to a fault. Yonder wants to be many things but ends up excelling at absolutly nothing, in fact I'd say its not even passable in many areas. Since the game set out to cover a varity of topics I'll cover where its failed in each catagory.
Exploration: While the world may feel somewhat vast at first you quickly realize its a vast emptiness. There is very little between point A and point B meaning the journey is less of an experience and you just end up wanting to get to your target as fast as possible. Many of the little side venues are nessecary but only for about .5 seconds then you run straight back to a town, this ends up artifically padding game length when you have to run half a mile through absolutely nothing to grab a ton of crap then run all the way back to craft that crap just to burn all of it instantly to get into a "new area" which is normally about 20 feet of space with 1 chest that gives you 1 to 2 of the 20 items you used to get there in the first place.
Because the game wanted its exploration to be so open ended, literally nothing that is blocked off from you is actually interesting to explore and is instead an extremely tiny, sometimes prettier, area with 1-2 chests or a few crates to smash and more often then not you won't get anything out of them that was really worth the trip.
Minor Exploration Spoiler: You have to burn a ton of wood to build two bridges to get to a "troll" village and the dialouge is obviously trying to play off of internet trolls but aside from one that says "games need guns" all of the "trolls" sound like they're just giving legitimate critcism the developers heard during production and should have taken into account before release.
Personal Message to the devs: Don't be so high and mighty. Its clear whatever you were given was legit criticism and you really should have at least considered it but because of where you've put it you seem to think tellling you that the "game lacked substance" was trolling when indeed, your game is very lacking in substance.
Crafting: O boy, the crafting. We fall somewhere between tedious and mind numbingly bad. Ok, maybe I'm just spoiled because I'm used to different crafting mechanics actually being somewhat related to one another. For example: If I told you there was basically a metal working crafter (construction) and that for Carpentry you needed nails, what would you say you needed to do to get nails? If you answered "Go create them with metal working" you're wrong, the correct answer is "trade them in limited supply from 1-2 traders that are on complete opposite ends of the map every few days." O, and its not just nails, every single crafting guild has several items that can only be bought in very limited supplies that are crucial for EVERY SINGLE CRAFTING RECIPE and that all sound like they should be craftable from the other guilds but hey, who needs something as useless as that right? Might as well artifically try and pad game time by literally blocking material gathering by limited stock merchants.
Other than that, a lot of the crafting is useless. Carpentry and Construction make literally the exact same items except for astehtic differences, Cooking is used for a woefully dull karma like system with specific residents thats not even nessecary and most of the fun stuff from Tailoring you just find on your own or you can buy from an end game shop. Brewing is somewhat related to tailoring but is really just mostly used to make stupid 1 shot fire work displays that are too resource intensive to care about and provide literally no benefit, not even a good firework display TBH.
Combat: There is none. Get over it. I know they tried to advertise this as if it had anything in common with "The Legend of Zelda" but it really doesn't. No dungeons or combat of any type, really shouldn't have been compared to it.
Farming: Dull. You put down a planter, you put 9 seeds in it and everything is automated from there, animals work exactly the same, trees work exactly the same. Everything else for your farm is just machines to help your craft certain materials from the Tinkers guild but I barely used them since the items those specific machines made were easily available elseware or simply weren't ever needed reallly.
Story: Non-existent. It kinda throws the "plot" at you last minute and instantly gives you the climax 2 seconds later. I think if we're looking at actual "story" quests theres about 6 and 3 of those are technically the same quest. If it wasn't for a few artifical barriers, you'd have the main story done in about 30 minutes. Other then that its pretty cliche, I guess I won't spoil it just incase you might care to see it but its really not much to write home about. My biggest complaint was they tried to end it with a "but theres a whole world out there to explore still, theres so much to do" when really there just isn't. I don't know, it just left a bad taste in my mouth.
Final Thoughts: Look, I've nearly 100% this game in 9 hours, theres really not much here. Its not like I didn't get side tracked, I tried to force myself to get side tracked, build up several farms and everything but theres just not much to get side tracked with. While trying to capture the identities of these different styles of game the devs lost sight completely of what they were doing and forgot to flesh out any of them. Theres barely anything to explore as almost everything is above ground already, farming is completely automated for you even the collection is all thrown nice and neat into a chest and the crafting is just insane tedium combined with absolutely no synergy. This feels so much like an early access title right now and whats bad is, seeing as this recieved a legitimate release on Playstation, chances are they aren't adding anything, they think its complete when I don't think things could be further from that.
Conclusion: If you really need something to just sit back and relax with for a few hours, I think you'll have fun with it but honestly, I just can't in good faith recommend it. The entire game just feels unfinished, more like a prototype then a full release even if it is half AAA pricing. The devs seriously need to expand on absolutely everything because right now its all so bare bones that you can't really get anything out of the systems and I just think its unfortunate that it's probably gonna stay that way. At best, its a disapointment.
Edits: I decided to add this which I at first did not want to add last night because I felt it was largely nitpicks but on the off chance the devs read this review, I want them to understand a few things they most likely should have done in order to help improve certain mechanics.
First: Construction should have been just "metal working" instead of being a copy paste of carpentry and it should have included better tools. These better tools should have either been used to gather rarer materials or given higher material yeild for the normal materials. Although minor this gives an actual feeling of progression. Realistically it should have been both. This also helps prevent burnout since you get all the tools within the first 30 minutes of play time if you go to the right areas.
Second: Some things NEED to be blocked off and you NEED to give me a reason to go there. At current, the biggest barrier was to the "troll" village and I got a few lines of self-rightous dialouge and some coins to buy cosmetics with and that wasn't just the biggest area but the densest area by far out of all the blocked off areas. The most expensive stone bridge which could take upwards of an hour just to get the materials for is literally a 10 foot by 10 foot platform with 1 chest that has a single backpack in it, why?

The story pulls no punches, neither glorifying nor demeaning the difficult lives its protagonists lead--just presenting them with brutal honesty and letting you reach your own conclusions. After the 10-or-so hours it might take you to gun through Vito's story, it's hard not to come away with the sense that there should have been more to do in this beautiful city. Yet while you might be disappointed with what Mafia II doesn't do, it's hard to be disappointed by what this excellent game does do: deliver fun shoot-outs and pockets of shocking brutality in a world you're delighted to be a part of.

I would advise taking the negative reviews with a very large pinch of salt. Lichdom is a decent game with an excellent crafting system. In fact this crafting system is the key to everything as to whether you get the best out of the game or not. The graphics are very nice and well optimised and even if you are, like me, one of those that tends to overestimate your cards abilities and slam everything as high as possible at the cost of framerate, there are FPS lock options at 30 and 60fps to limit any noticeable slowdown and stutter. The storyline is better than average, the acting and voice work likewise. RPG elements are there but limited so you can view the game overall as a cross between a FPS and an ARPG.
Most importantly, Lichdom has been made available in giveaways and super cheap Bundles meaning you can pick it up for free or near to free. A good example is the Fantasy Heroes Bundle on Bundlestars. As such it would be a real shame to miss out on it. Possibly not worth its full price but when you can get it cheaply it would be foolish not to. In fact just about every game in that bundle is good and you should snap it up while you still can.
*edit* As a side note I was saddened to note that after only 3 hours of play I had more completed achievements than over 80% of players. Meaning that most of those negative reviews are worthless.
A normal person with self-respect would have stopped playing by now. This game is like playing the exact same battle time after time with a slight change in topography.

The fluidity of the battlefield is AMAZING! It's like Quake with no jumping, which sounds dull but it's not. Spell crafting might take you a few misses, but you'll figure it out. As for the story? I have no idea what is going on, and I don't care. The characters might as well be all different bowls of the same porridge: dreary and unflavored.
Would I recommend this game? Yes, with reservations. THIS IS AN ARCANE SHOOTEM' UP. Not an rpg, or anything with a story taht you care about. It's good for blasting baddies and discovering new ways to make the bad guys deader.

I have attempted to finish this game 3 times now. Each time the same thing happens.
1. Oh wow, this game is really cool why did I stop playing before?
2. Well I'm sure I get stronger down the road, that fight only took so long because I'm still using basic spells.
3. Wow, these enemies are taking like 10 spell blasts each to go down, this sucks.
4. Oh great, another terrible extremely basic upgrade that is giving me a whopping 3 extra damage.
5. That boss took seven million years. I'm done.
I usually make it about 4~ hours before I quit out of annoyance. You are so pathetically weak that even trash mobs take spell after spell after spell to take down, with some elite enemies taking upwards of 20+ casts. The upgrade system is very cool because it allows you to kind of craft your own spell in a way, but every stat boost is so small it might as well not even exist. You are REQUIRED to cast multiple spell types per enemy in order to stack damage boosters, and in the heat of battle while you are doing your best to dodge everything it can become very disorienting to switch between all the different spell types and remember which order to do it in.
The game could be really good if it was refined to make spells less worthless. But as it stands, it's just tedious and annoying.

There is PvP, and for a man in Asia, it's really frustrating at times. A random player can walk up to you and disappear while killing you 3 times with a single move. The lag is at times unbearable, but I believe the developers will get it done, since this is still launch day.
It runs smoothly, except for the occasionally day to night cycle changes when you tone down the brightness. Just a trivial matter, though.
For keyboard and mouse users, prepared to get mind ♥♥♥♥ed if you played an excessive amount of For Honor like me. The controls can get a bit weird at times and frustrating, but you'll get used to it after an hour or so.
Overall, this is a fine game, and one that I'm glad I pre-ordered. I have faith in the developers to patch most of the game breaking bugs, and for the community to not be toxic and ledge people.

After about 13 hours of playing I can safely recommend this game. I am yet to play a game that offers this much customization to the core gameplay,aka combat in this case. Also connection has been absolutely perfect,I've played about 100 matches so far and I am yet to see any lag in 1v1 duels. Creating your own combat deck is insanely fun and it's actually really logical too. As long as you pay attention to what your moves actually do and the stance they end up in you can create a deck that changes to all 4 stances fluidly. Also it's just so rewarding to absolutely kick♥♥♥♥♥with the build you made yourself rather than having to look up meta builds in games like dark souls to win technically any other build out there as long as you play better than your opponent. This system is absolutely incredible,possibilities for different combat decks are almost infinite so every single one trick build has a counter. As someone who has won 100 or so matches and lost just 1 at the time of writing I think it's safe for me to say that making a well rounded build is a lot smarter than making a build that just does one thing over and over again. It might work on those who are really bad at the game but you'll get destroyed by anyone who knows what they're doing if you just button mash 2 abilities over and over again. And before anyone says that my build must be broken or smth because I'm quite simply not losing I can safely say that I could beat anyone using my exact build. No build is 100% bulletproof and everyone should know what their own builds are good at and what works against them. I used to like Carnivores. Not to love 'em or something but still like it. Now on Steam Sales there was this and I couldn't resist. After playing for like 2 hours, I can give my thoughts about the game.
The game offers us a trip to a planet inhabited by dinosaurs provided by a fictional hunting firm DinoHunt. Our job is simple. We get one of the available weapons (those are pretty limited to 3 kinds), get additional equipment like a camouflage and we are thrown into a prehistoric landscape. We have to stalk through jungle to hunt like 7 or 8 kinds of dinosaurs, including ferocious T-rex. Every kill is awarded with gems and score (depends on how many shots we took to take down the beast, what was the distance and stuff), which is a somewhat a currency in the game for opening new levels. With gems we pay for our equipment, weapons and license for a particular species of a dinosaur. We can hunt freely for every type we encounter, but only licensed dinosaurs will be in our thropy room. And that's pretty much it. We get the score quite fast so sooner or later we get access to new levels until we get it all and then the game loses it's replay value. That's pretty much all in terms of gameplay.
The graphics are nice but compared to other games it looks really decent. The dinosaurs are quite well detailed but I've seen better. Also beware to not turn on the advanced grass. It will slow ur  PC to a calculator mode from the stone age era.
Next thing is the sound. We get a simple, forgetable music in the background and the enviroment sounds which are mostly re-used stock sounds like crickets, wind sound and typical jungle uproars. In case of dinosaurs, we get really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ stock sounds, took from cartoons I guess. Really, in old carnivores games, there were better sounds than in this one.
Overall I would give the game 6/10. It's an good game for a dinosaur maniacs, but people who are not used to stalk'n kill games and are not into dinosaurs at all, should look for another game. I would highly recommend for the devs to add more dinosaur species (really? Only 2 carnivores? No Velociraptor? No Allosaurus? Shame...) and a larger variety of weapons. That way this game would have at least some replay value. At this point, it's just a decent dino-shooter.

The only area where the PC version is better is the headphone audio, which is definitely more chilling and better recorded.
I bought this game, but then I discovered the PSP version, and I just couldn't look at the PC version anymore.
Still, I'm not asking for refunds, just to support high quality VNs on PC, but I recommend the PSP versions far more (the upcoming 3ds version will be the definite version).
As for the game itself, its a very slow boiling horror story, it takes advantage of the long play time to lure players to invest emotional commitment to their characters before some are killed off. The results are far more terrifying than your typical gorefest, not to mention it explores deeper themes than simple creepy stories, meaning you'll remember the story for far longer than the likes of Alan Wake or Before Dawn or any Resident Evils (if that can still be considered a horror game)

First I want to say I am a hard core gamer. I have played many games with unimaginable amount of time spent yet I have not found the time to write a review for any of them. Then this game came along and I see all the negative and I just could not sit on the side lines any longer.
Be warned this is a long review and I reference other games if you don't know them then look em up so you know what I am talking about.
I have played World of Tanks(WoT) on PC and then I played World of Tanks Blitz(WoTB) on the tablet for more hours then I can count. I have spent 100's of dollars on both of those games. Now this game comes along and people are saying P2W? I beg to differ. I have in many occasions demolished those million gold tanks with my little Tier 1's How is it done? simple, if you like games like Starcraft and Warcraft 3 were micromanagement and I highly enfisize "team battle" is more important then just your 1 guy. Then this is the game you are looking for!
For those of you old classic gamers if you have played Shattered Galaxy then stop reading this review and start playing this game I garentee you will not be disappointed.
I have also seen and felt that rage of those missile launching artillery. many have claimed that they are so over powered. Well some of you need to learn to use your skills such as stealth go behind enemy lines do a blitz kreg and wipe em out! they have paper Armour and die super fast. Stop whining about it and do something about em.
If you liked games like Dawn of War 2 but you got tired of wiping out AI and stupid controlled computer bots then look no further this game will give you all the emotions of a good MOBA like League of Legends, yet you get to drive around in tanks! What more can you ask for? I know that certain tanks realistically would not perform in certain ways but this is a game and in order to make it balanced I understand many things had to have been changed to make it balanced. I love Real Time Strategy(RTS) and this game has filled that hole that I have been craving for a long time now. I plan to keep playing many many more hours.
Make sure to get the boost ability and do double boost and increase the range mobility is the biggest part of this game and a quick boost can save your life, time, and gold so you don't have to re-spawn. If used tactically you can boost strait into the enemy and confuse the crap out of them, this can let your team win
1 last tip if you are not willing to or can't afford to put in money into this game and support it. You can still kill those 1 million or even 2 million or even those elite platinum tanks. Simply buy multiple of the lowest tier tanks 4 of each would be good and when you get enough points to command more then one go with all 4 of them and swarm the enemy for the Zerg! Don't forget skills are the most important part of this game so use them and I mean use them on your team, by healing them and shields to block the enemy's rounds. This is a team game, play it as so. Doing this will give you more exp, witch gives you higher rank and then gives you more gold to buy cool stuff.
If you are worried about consumables running out I would not worry about it, I have almost never ran out because you get so many achievements and rewards that unless you are spamming them every second I doubt you will run out.
Good luck have fun and most important just remember it's only a game
Edit:
Level quickly tips:
Make sure to get the shield ability first and use this this ability on your teammates every time you use this ability on a teammate you will get 15 exp per a use.
Make sure you use the (Supply) instant repair kit you get 30 free ones every mission. Use them all on teammates and heal them you get 20 exp per a use
You can also use the field repair kit for another 20 exp. This heals the target for 500 hp over a period of time. However, if they take any damage of any kind it will stop the healing process
you can also get 20 exp from using nitro on teammates
Summary of abilitys and item usage on teammates
15 exp for shield ability
20 exp for instant repair
20 exp for field repair kit
20 exp for nitro speed
Level quick so you can control more tanks and then have more fun by using them correctly.
New tips and tricks for new players
For you new players make sure to stay on the battleline it's what the game is called you will get more exp just sitting on the battleline stopping the enemy from pushing the battleline then going across the line trying to kill enemy tanks.
I recommend to go full points into forward move speed as it will benefit you greatly if you are good at moving and shooting.
Wait for your red circle to become very small so that when you shoot you do a critical hit. With some tanks, this can provide 50%+ damage and when you are shooting a tank from behind that has no Armour you can cause some BIG damage.
Stay as a team or go to the sides <- -> were there is less people and push the line, remember stay on the battleline push the line.
If you are using multiple tanks the commands are z,x,c,r
z = tanks move and attack (They will move to your spot and attack anything in it's path, if you select a unit with this command they will focus and follow that target when it is died they will act as "c" follow)
x = move and do not attack (They will move to your location and not attack)
c = Follow your main tank (You can have your units follow you, they will not shoot anything while following)
r = Stop and hold this position (They will stop immediately and not shoot or do anything, Honestly they should stop and shoot but it's the developers that need to change that)
If you double right click on one of your other tanks you can switch between witch one you are controlling directly.
You can also use the F1, F2, F3, F4 when you select one individually this way and right click on the map they will do a "x" move and do not attack command. However, once they reach that location and stop they will defend that spot. Meaning anyone that comes within range they will engage and follow until that unit is destroyed. They will then move back to the location that you commanded them to go. You can control multiple tanks and send them to guard different locations this way.

I am recommending this game, but take that with a grain of salt. I've seen several reviews comparing this game to games like stardew valley, harvest moon, or zelda and I have no idea why. Do not expect this game to feel like any of those titles because you will be disappointed. (honestly it feels more like any given mmo, but without the ability to do any of it online with your friends)
So up top, positives: I do like it! It's cute and entertaining, and it is pretty relaxing not having to murder every adorable animal that crosses my path. And the animals are really adorable, I've loved every single one I've come across. Cats make for an adorable collectable as do the sprites that have to be rescued for the main quest.
And unfortunately on the negative side: The plot isn't interesting enough to hold my focus, if i even understand which quest is the main quest and not one of the innumerable fetch quests I've picked up from a generic npc somewhere that I've forgotten. And speaking of forgetting, The farm that you own is so forgettable that I can barely remember where it is half the time (again I have to say nothing like stardew valley. I'm so baffled by that comparison). I learned how to craft some things for my farm but I already was given all those things by an npc for doing yet another fetch quest and so crafting has been just a bunch of nothing for me, other than a backpack full of items that i'm never really sure if i'll need becuase what if it learn how to craft something cool later? Character customization is done almost entirely through exploring or trading, which means my character always looks incredibly dumb. And since I've touched on crafting and customisation that me to the trade system which constant hassle beacuse nothing is worth anything solid. Some traders will give insanely more "money" for generic items but they'll have nothing that I have any interest in at all and money is used very loosely because there is no actual currency it's a full barter system where everything is given a monetary value but can only be traded for other items. And just as another little annoyance, buildings are just there for nothing, they can't be gone inside and npcs live their entire lives just standing outside of an impossible to enter house.
Overall, a lot of things in game have felt imcomplete, dialogue is always very short and clipped, and I feel there were a lot of little things I could nitpick, but I've pointed out what I thought were the biggest problems. To me the game really feels like it's still in early access, so much so that I actually had to check while playing to make sure it wasn't. A lot of negatives for a recommended review, but like I stated at the beginning, I do like this game. Exploring the world is fun, the art style is cute and vibrant and walking around and seeing what the world has to offer is a good time. But it's definitely got a lot of problems and if you plan on buying it you should really be ready to take it on a test run to see if it's actually a game that you would want to keep playing.
TLDR: not like stardew valley, feels like an early access game, but can still be adorable and fun if it's the kind of game you're into.

With the Community Patch, Gothic 3 is one of the most ambitious, challenging, and varied RPGs that I've played. It is beautiful and engrossing. It blends the grittiness of Witcher with the scope of Skyrim and just doesn't quit. The character progression is superbly balanced. The map design is superlative and gets you excited to explore. I haven't seen better. You will die, and die, and die but it never feels unfair. This game is bizarrely underrated.

Do not buy this game, not even if it's on sale. People say it's the best RPG in the world, even better than Skyrim because it has such an amazing, large and deep world to play with. That may be! Except the combat mechanics are literally the worst I've ever had to endure in a video game. Melee combat is horrific. When you try to block an attack it's 50/50 whether it'll actually block it or not. It's not supposed to be 50/50 - if you block it's supposed to block - but the game is so buggy it doesn't always register. You can't tell when an enemy is going to attack because animations are so stiff and poorly done, so it's almost impossible to know when to block. The enemy, on the other hand, will block all your attacks with total efficiency. If you want to play as a melee character, this leaves you with no choice but to approach an enemy and furiously mash the left mouse button to attack over and over and hope you win, which is 50/50. Quite often the enemy will hit you and make you stumble, putting you in what I call a "death spin" which you can't get out of. This is where the enemy keeps stunning you with each hit, meaning you can't retaliate and eventually die.
Furthermore, the game is buggy as hell. Even with the community patch this game is horrendously buggy. I had to restart 3 or 4 times to get past the first part because after I had killed all the enemies in the little village (by furiously mashing the left mouse button because there's nothing else you can do) because you have to talk to this guy to advance the story afterwards, except when I tried to talk him he just said "talk later". After 3 or 4 restarts he finally talked to me.
Archery is even worse. All you have to do is stand on a spot that breaks the enemy AI (which is basically on any kind of rock or tree stump because the AI is awful) and the enemies will begin slowly walking away from you because they have no way of getting to you. So you can wipe out nests of 100 goblins by standing on a rock, even though under normal circumstances 2 or 3 at once would be a challenge.
I can't recommend this game. It's absolutely awful.

Aarklash is, for once, a $20 game worth $20 (though I got it for $5, yay).
Prior to this I had a pretty low opinion of pause-based RT tactical games.  Usually the pause feature is just there to cover up for the fact that the game is a clickfest with too much information and too many commands poorly presented or hidden in menus.
Aarklash has created the perfect pause-based gameplay.  The streamlined controls, interface, and action queue system present all the information you need without overloading your senses and all the control you want without forcing you to micromanage every single attack.
The enemies are billiantly created, with complementary abilities and ingenius passives that force you to examine each enemy group, develope new strategies to counter their abilities, and constantly watch for them to start casting so you can pause, check what spell they're using, and decide how/whether to interrupt or dodge.  You WILL get that feeling of "oh my god I just pulled through that by the hair of my teeth" that you get when you take an intimidating clusker-f**k and turn it around through skilled reactions and battle control.  It's pretty rewarding, not to mention fun.
The player's abilities are fairly well done as well, though I wish there are been a bit more depth.  You only get 21 points, which is enough to max out 2 of the 8 lines and almost one of the others.  In some cases this forces you to make tough choices and can lead to different gameplay, but often there seems (to me) to be a clear winner.
Items appear to all be procedurally generated with three levels of rarity and the ability to recycle ones you don't want for  new highest quality items.  On the one hand, it gives you some of the constant upgrades you get from a rng gear game, but on the other hand you get so much gear it doesn't really matter.  That's all good, except the game also has no gear you might consider "special", so you never really get the feeling of having found anything cool or worth keeping.  Also, many of the stat mechanics are unknown as well (such as armor), which means it's hard to even decide what to use.
There are a lot of puzzles in the game, and they are generally fun and at least semi-challenging (difficulty varies widely).
The story isn't bad, but lacks depth.  The characters are well flushed out, especially given how limited the dialogue is.  However, several of them are pretty much useless (Bo Lahm, for example is a crappy hybrid horrible at both tanking and damage).  You'll have to use each of them for a little while, but for most of the game you'll use only the same 4 characters.
Overall, it's a OK game on top of a fantastic combat system.  They could definitely have made it great with a bit more work, but I definitely recommend the game to any tactical RPG players.

Edited review.
Basement is a fun management game that puts you in the shoes of a drug dealer attempting to expand his empire in an urban setting.
Although still in Early Access, it is fairly playable in its current state, with each subsequent update seemingly focused on extending the game's already considerable playability further.
The game requires you to acquire buildings to setup your operations and hire staff to manufacture and distribute your product (as well as hiring muscle to protect it).
In addition, you must keep up with the demand of junkies, while diversifying in what drugs you make/sell. This increases your revenue, enabling you to acquire new buildings and expand your empire further, but also makes your business more prone to police raids.
Buying transport to transport goods between premises is an option provided you have a garage, providing further depth to your manufacturing and distribution network, and forcing you to think about designating premises to perform particular functions: manufacture, distribution, storage etc.
Each character in the game has a set of stats which indicates things attributes such as: health, damage, ability to sell drugs, ability to manufacture etc. which level up over time as the attribute is used. This enables you to specialise your employees in order to maximise their effectiveness at their given tasks.
Aesthetically the game's pixel graphics are well-done and quite charming in their presentation.
The minimal soundtrack compliments the atmosphere and immersion the chosen pixel art style affords, and I look forward to future updates that expand out the content even further.
At the moment the game is currently only a sandbox mode, but the developer has mentioned future updates will also include other traditional game modes.
Should you buy the game now in its current state, you will get something that is currently playable, but will also be contributing to its further enhancement which is en exciting prospect given how fun it already is.
Lets just hope the updates keep coming :)

When an alien ship crash lands on Earth and immediately sets up a force field around itself, its up to an elite squad to infiltrate the Anomaly and stop the alien incursion.  This isn’t tower defense, this is tower offense.  This is Anomaly: Warzone Earth.
In a total reversal of the normal genre tropes, you will guide a squadron of tanks through the streets of Baghdad and Tokyo, blasting away at the stationary towers along the path.  At any time, you can redirect your team to take advantageous routes, avoiding enemies (or more likely, catching them off-guard so you can collect that sweet, sweet money) and attempting to reach objectives.
There are six different units, each of which can be upgraded three times.  You don’t directly control them, however, you simply set their route through the levels.  You have control over a commander, who can sprint across the battlefield, drawing fire and laying down special abilities like smokescreens, decoys, and repair rings.  These are key to keeping your squad alive so they can blow up all the alien towers.   Luckily, for the most part, these power-ups are airdropped frequently.
The game progresses quite linearly, alternatively giving you new units and new towers to test your wits against.  The storyline isn’t much to write home about, we’ve all seen alien invasions before, though the voice acting is pretty good.  Each level has a series of sub-objectives that need to be completed in order to advance, though in general blowing up all the enemies will be in your advantage.  There are end-of-level bonuses given out for being efficient (lowest expenses), ruthless (most kills) and direct (shortest route).
The visuals do a good job of mixing things up, even in Baghdad where everything is just a brown and beige desert.  The enemies are unique and bright, and your units are distinct enough to easily be recognized.   This game plays alright with a mouse and keyboard, but it was originally made for Xbox 360 and the control show.  Pick up a gamepad and the game really flows well.  The controls are snappy and intuitive, making the hectic battles much more manageable.
The audio cues are very nicely done, as it’s easy to tell different enemy attacks apart.  Your squadron will often call out for your assistance if they are under fire, asking for repairs or smoke screens if things get too hectic.  The music is a touch generic, consisting mainly of military fight music in both Middle Eastern and Asian themes, depending on where the level is set, but it gets you in the mood for tanks blowing up aliens, so no complaints from me.
The game progresses nicely in difficulty, slowly ramping up the challenge as new and unusual enemies that require new tactics are constantly thrown your way.  Sometimes certain skills will be taken from you, or you’ll have no choice but to walk right into a trap you can see coming.  I just wish the campaign was a little bit longer so I would have had a chance to grow into my strategies a little more, rather than constantly being off-balance.  I have these awesome tanks to play with, let me feel powerful for a while before overwhelming me again!
This was a fun game!  It is full of unique gameplay that is very easy to understand, yet challenging to complete.  The PC version is a completely different campaign than the mobile version (which is also available separately on Steam) so if you can’t get enough Anomaly, there’s an entire extra game to play (not to mention the sequels!)

The graphics are beautiful, and the game runs just fine with all the eye candy maxed out on my AMD 1090T 3.2 GHz 6-core, ATI Radeon R9 280X-DC2 TOP, 16 GB DDR3 RAM machine.
You may find warnings about AMD/ATI systems on this title, but you don't have to worry.  Simply set all your graphics options in game, including AA and AF, and then add the game to your Catalyst Control Center and set everything to "Use Application Settings".  You won't have any problems.
If you're looking for just straight forward, uncomplcated dinosaur hunting with beautiful graphics, this will do it.

Here's my First Impressions & Review video:
I actually love the hand drawn looking art in this game and think this is a pretty cool little casual RPG that isn't too hardcore, but pretty fun with tons of NPCs, tons of questions, and lots and lots of loot to be had.
You have 3 save slots for up to 3 different game saves or characters to play.  Great for people that might want to allow another member of their house to play the same game and have their own game save slot.
You start off getting to customize your character tree with all kinds of options to make yourself look unique and interesting.  Then you are brought into a huge 2D world with nice hand drawn art and other people and creatures.  Moving your tree avatar to the left or right side of the screen will load in the next screen and if you move with a door just behind you, you can move up (W key) to move through the door as long as it is unlocked.  Items can be accessed and NPCs can be talked to by hitting your E key by default when you move near them.  Attacking a baddie can be done by simply clicking your left mouse button.  Space jumps, and shift allows you to sprint but uses your stamina which will recover over time when you stop sprinting.  Note that all of these keys CAN be customized in the options to what ever you prefer.
I gave this game a 74% out of 100, with most of the points knocked off only because the game I feel is just a little over-priced at it's regular $9.99 USD price tag.  Still, a good score though if you are looking for a casual RPG or perhaps one that might interest and engage children.
Recommended for sure unless you are expecting Skyrim or Dark Souls for your money here.  :-)

Battleline: Steel Warfare is what i call a certain unique game, i dont think theres any other like this one thats has big multiplayer matches and free2play.

My current ign in Battleline is Haraquiri.
First of all, since its a free2play, theres the big question "pay2win"?
On my current gaming experience in the game, no it isnt at all since you can buy pretty much everything ingame, im rather disapointed that there isnt any "skins" for people to support this game but rather packs of tanks that you can buy with ingame money.
Currently i like the matchmaking, it may seem "unfair" but you only enter a match when someone of around the same level as you enters the enemy team at the same time as you.
I am currently using the official instaled game from the games website so regarding the conections on steam, i cannot say much about it.
Tips for newbies:
The comunity on this game is a rare one, everyone tries to help each other without actualy any flamming, its highly advisable to check the minimap and chat very often.
Teamwork is essential on this game, your skills and items can also be used/affected on your allies.
Currently the tutorial in the game is realy boring but quick&important, just have patience on it.
You gain a good amount of gold on the beggining to buy what tank you wish for, but please check that you have the required crew for it.
A good way to win items and gold is to buy new tanks and do its achievments ingame.
If you are using a main tank+ ligh, if you lose your main, you can just return with you light tank to a spawn base and wait 2 or 3 min to respawn it again.
Use your researchers only on your favorite skill.
Remenber that this game is called "Battleline".
The current aspect of balance that you need to realize
Artilary:
Some say they are OP because they are very usefull for slow targets and huge enemy blobs, perfect to counter when youre outnumbered.
But its catch, they die easily by 2 or 3 hits, are extremly slow, without counting the 4 hour limited arty you get from training mission, the other ones take at least 40ish min to respawn, that means you can be playing 3 or 4 matches before you get to use your arty again.
Regarding gameplay situations that need some fixing.
Theres still some work needed on the parthfinding, your tank may "dance" if you stay too close to a edge of the map or a building.
Companies take a huge amount of time to find an available match.
Theres other things that i havent touched but these are the most important info i consider about this game.
Overall i would put this game on the same shell as the other rare free2play games that arent pay2win but can still have some small issues, its an unique genre of its own that is problably not for every type of gamer.

This is the first time I have written a review so im going to just start out by talking about the game then I will get into a more pro/con format later in.
I played castle story back when it was just out of the prototype stage and there were many problems. two of the biggest problems were the path finding of the units and the camera's controls, everything else was injoyable. I have taken over 2 year break from this game. After the break I have come back to islands (maps) that are 10x as big as the "first island", two new game modes conquest (capture the point) and invasion (wave survival), a normal camera control system and enemys that you have to defend against. To add on to all that devs are getting ready to launch a multiplayer update where we can share control with friends or battle against one another (but as thats not in yet I will keep that out of my mind for the rest of the review). The game mode conquest is not very injoyable to me but the invasion mode is very challenging but fun so I'm going to focus on invasion. In invasion you start out with a few workers, a knight, an archer and your crystal (homebase) so you stright away get to work setting jobs and delgating how many workers you want doing diffrent jobs such as chopping trees for wood, working the iron mines, working in your querry for stone to make bricks or building your stronghold. Now building is a little unique you have to build your structures one brick at a time (you can click and drag so its not tedious) which means you can end up with a stronghold that can take multiple hits of explosive barrels or one. You can make you stronghold tall or wide its up to you but you do have to make sure you put supports under your structures so that your building doesn't collapse on its self. So I would say that castle story is a game that has seen a lot of growth and is at a stat were its fun to play.
Some pros and cons:
If you have the money to spare I think castle story is a game you should pick up.

I bought this game in February of 2014, and it has come a long, long way since that time. I remember buying a copy, and buying another copy for a friend of mine, and we both were very impressed with the functionality and gameplay straight off the bat. Early on, it was a little rough around the edges, but seeing as the devs are keeping it updated and adding more and more as time goes on, I have no doubt it will keep getting better and better. The multiplayer is pretty cool, fairly functional with a few small bugs, but I'm going to chalk those up to be the fact that my friend was hosting the server in Michigan and I was connecting from Arizona. The bugs I mentioned were buildings popping in and out of existance, Bricktrons popping in and out of existance (both of these item popping into and out of existance bugs reset after a server restart. Nothing ingame was lost.), and crashes occationally when my friend would stop the server.
As of right now, 05,16,2016, the multiplayer gameplay is a little bland. There's not much to do other than try to make cool castles and watch as bricktrons dig their way into the ground, then eventually seal themselves in their own mines. There is no PVP combat yet with the warriors, but you can still lop arrows at your friend's worker bricktrons when he sends them over to your base to say hello. BUT, the devs Shatojon and Evax livestreamed a new work in progress update teaser with co-op corruptron combat and base building 3 days ago on 05,13,2016. I can't wait until they release it. I will update this review with my thoughts after I have explored the update, but my first impressions from seeing the livestream are very positive. A co-op bricktron combat alongside co-op base building is exactly what I wanted from this game.
Overall, I am very pleased with my $20 investment. Some people tend to say that every hour of playtime should considered to be about a dollar, and if you come up short on hours spent playing, then it's a bad investment. I personally don't think that's a very good idea of how you should look at the picture. I see it as this: if the game is fun, then it's a good investment, if the game is bad, it's a bad investment. You'll never know if it's good or bad until you invest. Don't take my opinion as the gospel, nor should you take anyone else's opinion as the gospel, since we all have different opinions. If the game looks fun to you, invest, if you don't want to, don't. Just don't whine and moan when the game isn't perfect even though it says right above the "Add to cart" button that the game isn't perfect and that it is still in early access. Don't♥♥♥♥♥♥on the developers who are making this game for a living for not completing the game quick enough. They're taking their time to make the game as perfect as they want it to be, updating it and keeping in contact with the customers. Hell, the developer Shatojon even added me and sent me a message asking my opinion on the game. Has any AAA game developer gone out of their way to actually talk one on one with a customer before? Did Ubisoft go out of their way to ask their consumers' opinions on Assassin's Creed Unity after it was released broken? Nope. The only thing Ubisoft's CEO has said was that ALL Steam users and all PC users are pirates, and that he doesn't give a ♥♥♥♥ if the game is broken for us.  Would you, the consumer, really rather have a broken game on release and a CEO of the company you're buying the content from telling you to get bent because he's an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, than a game functional in early access and a group of devs who really bust their asses with a game they want people to enjoy? Seriously?

I'm a fan of this company's Hidden Object/Adventure Games. I often found myself wondering what it would be like if they just buckled down and made a straight Adventure Game, unburdened by the need to shoe-horn in seemingly-pointless HOP elements. Now I know. I wish I didn't.
This game is a mess. Poorly translated, plodding & often nonsensical, with a wet thud of a finale, "Parallels Cross" feels like a HOP/Adventure game that was half-finished and rushed out the door to meet an artificial deadline...only to have Dave the intern forget to unlock all the HOP elelments. It's dull, the pacing makes no sense ("My son is missing! I know where he is! So let me just spend potentially HOURS solving this out-of-the-blue number sequence puzzle I have no reason to believe is in any way related to his mysterious disappearance rather than smashing in the window and chasing after my missing son!"), the puzzles are EXTREMELY tedious, and for the first time EVER in any of their games I found myself skipping puzzles just to get through the dang thing. Don't bother with this one. It's a dud, plain and simple. Clearly they have no clue how to make a straight adventure game. Let's hope they stick with the hybrid games from here on out.

This game is squeaking by with a tentative positive rating; it's one of many that make me wish there was an in-between "meh" option.
Graphically it's pretty, puzzles aren't terribly hard, and I enjoy the map system that tells me where I've completed so I'm not wandering in circles.  If anything, the puzzles are a little too easy if you're a veteran at minigames.
There is nothing that stands out about the sound quality, but there is no voice work which is a little bit of a turn-off with so many games nowadays having voice acting.
Plot is formulaic but not terribly so.
The major thing I'd want people to know about this is that despite the screenshots looking like your basic HO genre game, there's a reason why it's not tagged that way.  There is not a HO aspect to this game at all.  Essentially it's a point-and-click game with puzzles, wearing the user interface of a hidden-object game.
My biggest complaint would be the playtime; I finished the entire game in about 90 minutes and there is no bonus content or achievements (or any other extras or frills) that would induce me to play it again.  It is definitely NOT worth the full price due to the short playtime and lack of complexity.
However, if you can grab it on sale, it's not a terrible purchase if you take into account the things mentioned above,  You're not going to get a really top-of-the-line game, but there are certainly worse options, especially if you (like myself) have practically exhausted your supply of similar games.
This game is at alpha stage, definitely not complete or ready for release.  No point in trying to play it.

My ship was caught in a fierce storm, and I stood at the bow, helpless against the ravaging seas. Thunder crackled in the sky, waves crashed around me, and then everything went black. I assumed that I was dead. “Good grief, Tom,” I thought to myself, “three minutes into this game and you’ve already managed to drown the little fellow.” Then my screen faded back into focus and relief washed over me. Aaerie, the spirit guardian of the island I washed up on, decided to give me a second chance at life.
Yonder is an adorable, friendly for all ages, game. The main aspects of Yonder are exploration and crafting. Players can purchase and customize farms and collect resources from their animals and crops as well as gather resources from the environment. The resources can then be traded to townsfolk to help complete focused objectives.
Compared to its contemporaries, Yonder is a fairly shallow game. Obviously geared at younger gamers, the crafting system in Yonder isn’t as complex or item-dense as I expected it to be. With that said, in addition to being shallow, the game is, at times, vague; it can be tedious to try and figure out how to craft/find a certain resource (where are you, Glue??). Yonder just always felt like it was created for children who have loads more free-time to gallivant around in a video game, than I do. Which is fine, but not necessarily what I am looking for in a game.
Almost every quest in Yonder is a fetch quest. “Go collect X of this resource, and Y of that resource, then bring them back here.” If it weren’t for how gorgeous Yonder’s island is, and how fun it is to explore that beautiful wilderness, I wouldn’t view my time with the game as favorably as I do.
Tucked away into every corner of Yonder’s island are treasure chest with cosmetic goodies or rare resources. Lost kittens are the game’s collectible and every biome has its group of missing kittens to find. Exploring the island is very worthwhile and I always found myself wondering, “Hmm, I wonder what’s just around that corner?”
Lots of people seem to want to compare Yonder to Stardew Valley and Zelda. It’s neither one of those games. It lacks the depth and replayability that Stardew Valley has, and while it’s a pretty, open-world game, the land is vacant of enemies to battle or puzzles to solve beyond finding a particular resource needed to complete a quest. In Yonder you simply gather, craft, trade, and collect. Rinse and repeat.
I’m going to go ahead and recommend Yonder; it’s not a bad game, and the things I disliked about it are based on my personal taste, rather than about the quality of the game. Ten hours in the game and I found nothing mechanically wrong with Yonder. I’m happy to say it’s a very solid game and Prideful Sloth certainly have created something to be, well, prideful of.
Recommended for: young gamers and players looking for a kind-hearted, calm game to explore for a few nights.
Not recommended for: players looking for the excitement of Zelda or the depth/replayability of Stardew Valley.

This is a difficult game to review. If I could, I'd put this game into a neutral category. This is the kind of game that will polarize people into love or hate. I feel that a month or two of refinement, additional assets and play testing, could have elevated this game into something much greater than 7/10.
The negatives, in order of what was most noticeable:
- Each character has 4 skills to choose from. You only gain 1 skill point per level and most of the time, you will put the point into an existing skill. Therefore, for the first 10 levels, the skills don't tend to vary combat that much. This is boring. I never felt a sense of elation, that comes with leveling in MMO RPGs or single player RPGs.
Although I like the branching nature of the skill tree ( which modifies the effect, of the skill slightly ), the lack of skills feels RPG-light compared to a conventional RPG where clerics and mages might have 6-9 different spells.
Both your hero and skill points cap at level 20, which means that of the 4 skills, one was designed to be a dead end skill by the developers, since mathematically you will only have 1 default point in that particular skill. I'll give you a hint and say that some of the buffs and debuffs are a waste of casting time and mana, considering that the game focuses on DPS, stunlocking and healing.
It costs 3 skill points to respec your skill tree, which is too expensive.
Although I liked the strange, unique and avant-garde mechanics of the tank having to spend hit points, to perform skill actions, it does not work work very well for the first 5 levels, since she doesn't have a large enough health pool, to perform many actions. Similarly, the cleric does not regenerate mana and has to steal health from her companions, in order to generate magic points. She has to almost kill her companions, in order to heal them, which is amusing but likewise, doesn't really work for the first 5 levels or so ( this is a balance issue ). The amusing irony is that the mage ends up being the best, most versatile healer in the game.
- The tactical combat side of the game is, for the most part, tedious. There are probably only around 20 different monsters to fight which is simply not enough for an action RPG game. This game would need, at a bare minimum 50 different monsters. Something on the scale of 100 different monsters, would drastically elevate this game. Compared to the Dungeons and Dragons monster manual, this game is sorely lacking!
Combat consists of figuring out which opposing control wizard to stunlock, taking out the cleric and DPSing the enemy. Then you have to cross your fingers and hope that the RNG ( random number generator ) Gods are in your favour. Battles are usually a landslide, there are very few, close battles. You either efficiently dispatch the enemies or you unfortunately lose an ally, who ends up face down in the dirt and then you have to try and struggle to get a team-mate to revive him. The character doing the reviving will come under fire, which will delay the reviving, each time he takes a hit. I usually play games on the hardest difficulty levels but I had to set the difficulty to medium. The only difference is that on the harder difficulty levels, your allies will end up face down in the dirt, which increases the chances of a party wipe, then the game automatically ends and you have to reload the game and fight out the same battle. The harder difficulty levels are extraordinarily tedious and resemble the kind of grind in an MMO. Medium ( the default difficulty ) was too easy for me, so I never managed to find a happy equilibrium.
- The environments for Act 1 and 2 were bland. Act 1, the wilderness was the worst and gave the false impression of open world exploration. Realistically, for the first 5-10 levels, there is a set path to follow, in terms of finding treasure chests and being able to fight monsters at the level you are at. The only way to figure out the path, is to take the wrong turn, wipe and reload. This is tedious. The game environment becomes almost completely linear in Act 2 and 3, which is the way that Act 1 should have been. I did like the art direction for Act 3.
The positives:
+ I immediately liked the characters, plot, voice acting and dialogue. These are the aspects of the game that kept me playing.
+ I enjoyed the puzzles in Act 2 and Act 3. Each puzzle takes 5-10 minutes to figure out. If you don't like puzzle games then this game is not for you.
+ The orchestrated music was appropriate.
+ I enjoyed the part where you gained 4 additional characters and the game forced you to use them to explore. I wish that the game had had more of that.
+ The combat and skill tree does get more varied and interesting around level 13 ( which is relatively late in the game ).
Miscellaneous:
Examples of ARPGs ( action role playing games ) that I would recommend: "Freedom Force" and the sequel, "Freedom Force vs the 3rd Reich". Both of those games were fantastic 9/10 for the first and 10/10 for the second.

From your income you can upgrade your rooms, build new ones, start digging underground for a larger basement (which means more room for rooms), hire people to grow or mix your drugs, sell or transport said drugs, or keep your people safe from angry addicts and police raids. Or you could send them out to other buildings and expand your business through some...aggressive negotiations...
The game looks really nice and I think the choice for low resolution graphics has payed off in this case. There isn't much in terms of guiding new players into the game, and it feels more like a sandbox, but there is a sound foundation for what can become a great game, regardless of what anybody may think about drugs.
I actually feel inclined to writing a beginners guide, but the game IS actually really easy to pick up, as long as you don't fear losing the first few games figuring it out.
Definately has potential.

A celebration of Sonic's past and present, you take control of Sonic and his younger self, named Classic Sonic, through reimagined levels from all across his career (up to 2011, at least). It's a blast to play despite its short length, its graphic have aged like wine, and best of all, there are mods you can download for new experiences!
Classic Sonic's levels play similarly to the original Genesis trilogy, and although it's not a 100% recreation like the more recent Sonic Mania is, the heart and soul the classics are here and intact. Meanwhile, Modern Sonic's levels are best described as being like roller coaster rides with alternate paths galore. Make no mistake, you'll still get from point A to point B, but knowing which route is the fastest is key to achieving the best possible time in both Classic and Modern styles.
There's also (mostly) optional side missions you can play, but they vary in quality from being brilliant to tedious. It's "mostly" optional because you have to do at least 3 missions in each set of 3 levels to progress to the next boss fight; but you're free to pick and choose which ones you would like to do as long as they fall within that specific era of games.

I tried to like this, I really did.  The game looks pretty good and the concept is good, but it's just not very fun.  The spell crafting system is nice and provides some customization to better suit your play style.  The story is weak, which would be fine if the combat system was the main focus and was good.  It's not.  I think hands down the most glaring flaw is that both you and the enemies are all just damage sponges.  Combat feels slow and a bit clunky.  You just chuck spell after spell at the enemy who ignores the fact you are pelting them and hit you back.  There is no AI to be found here.  You glitch all the time when you take damage, resulting in you raising your hands in front of your face and waving around for a few seconds rather than casting.  I can understand if they want enemy attacks to interrupt you, but they do not convey this well by not properly programming the model animations aka your flailing arms.  There are not many monsters that appear per spawn, as they seem to be relying on it taking a LONG time to kill them, rather than making the spawns contain more enemies and be placed more interestingly.  YOU CAN'T JUMP!  I really hate this.  You will see easy ways to progress, but cannot hop a few inches or climb the smallest rocks.  This tears me out of emersion a LOT.  It turns your adventure to a very "on rails" experience.  There are huge swaths of empty land scape.  You really get a feeling of isolation, even when running through places like a city.  Is this game supposed to be in a post-apocalyptic setting?  I can’t see anything on the store page or in the story to indicate this, but that’s the feeling they convey.  A final note is that this game crashes pretty frequently.  It just freezes and sits there staring at you until you end the process.  I have played countless games both indie and AAA that can go from beginning to end without a lockup and crash.  This game I can I think at longest went 45 minutes before an issue would arise.
Overall, I cannot recommend this game.  Not even steeply discounted or in a bundle.  This may “press the right buttons” for some people, but not for me.  I have seen other games do essentially everything this game does better.

Lichdom Battlemage is essentially a linear hallway-based first person shooter, but instead of shooting guns you’re shooting magical spells. That’s sort of an odd concept. What’s even odder is how all of the advertisements tried making the game look more like some sort of open brawler instead of the narrow linear experience it is.
The gameplay is alright. For a while. It’s extremely slow-paced for a first person shooter, but the placement and selection of your spells and constant action of it all keeps it very intense and engaging. It’s single player so unfortunately you can’t bring anyone along to fight by your side, and honestly that is exactly what this game needed. The game likes to spam you with the exact same enemies over and over and over as you drudgerously pace through spell upgrades in a surprisingly in-depth customization system that I didn’t even try to wrap my head around and instead just let it upgrade things for me, which I realized is actually a pretty bad idea because it takes any tiny upgrade it can get, even if it sacrifices a boatload of effect damage for 2 more base dps.
The graphics of this game are pretty damn good looking if a little hard to immerse yourself into with your floating hands which shadows reveal to literally be held up in front of you like an idiot at all times. The sound effects and music are nothing memorable. They get the job done.
The story is...well, it’s a story. Basically you pick a lusty-for-vengeance male protagonist or a ♥♥♥♥♥y ♥♥♥♥ everyone female protagonist and whichever you don’t pick becomes a useless scout that gives you information so useless that even the game makes fun of them. The story is boring and so rare that there’s no motivation to really grind through the slow paced boring levels. Ultimate bad guy corrupting the lands? Yeah ok, I’ll find the same thing in a different game but with better mechanics, easily.
Overall this game is not worth your time. I give it a 4/10. It has some solid mechanics.It’s almost an average game, but average games are fun. Lichdom Battlemage is not a fun game if you’ve ever played any good shooter or RPG before, as this game tries to be both, but manages to be neither.

Very good remake of one of my favourite games. I dare say remake because while it has the same feeling and style as the original, it is quite a different game. The visuals have obviously been significantly improved since the original and there are many things to upgrade and buy using this new gem currency. You can use the gems for so many things, like buying dino licences, purchasing different weapons, upgrading those weapons, buying equipment to make hunting easier, buying upgrades to your character such as running faster, being more difficult to smell, hear or see. You can also buy upgrades for your M.I.S.T, like a bigger dino spotting range, a dino roar decoy to make them come closer to you, and being able to call the drone faster for capture of dead dinos and evacuation. And none of these require you to spend real money, all you have to do is earn gems by killing dinos. There is also another currency called Score, which lets you explore new maps and allows you to buy the licences to more dinos using your gems. If I havent made it clear enough, there is a ton of replayability to this game, and if that isn't enough, there are also 12 achievements to unlock if you are an achievement hunter. The only gripes I have about this game is that, while the optimization isn't terrible by any means, it has clearly been ported from the PS3 version of this game, and i myself had to turn down the settings a tad to maintain a steady 60fps. Another small gripe is that there are only 6 dinos in this game, while the original had over a dozen, but Its not a big deal. In conclusion, if you love hunting games, dino games or are just looking for a fun game to pass the time, for just £10.99 this game meets and exceeds those expectations.

In The Adventures of Tree (TAoT) you play as a Formonger named Tree with a mission to fight the Florps (or not, depending on the choices you made in the game) in the land of Formagetus. Before you head in, there are 3 character slots for you to experiment with under the "Accounts" option in the main menu, each one of them contains an auto-saved character of yours for you to play around with your in-game choices that may or may not affect the ending. As I’ve mentioned, this game doesn’t seem to have a manual save option around, so most of your progress will be auto-saved, which I can’t find myself liking the idea, because that means that if you’ve picked the wrong choice at a point of time, there’s no going back unless you make a different choice with a different character.
Right at the start, the game presents a very standard character creation, nothing too fancy. Once you’ve made your log of Tree, there will be a small window asking if you would like to go through the tutorial. If you’ve missed it, you can always press the in-game hotkey H to bring up “Help” at any time to learn the shortcuts. TAoT doesn’t appear to have a control mapping option available, but the controls aren’t too bad, as it essentially follows the standard WASD and arrow keys to move around. As soon as you’ve been dropped within the realm, there are 3 bars on the top left consists of your general health points, stamina bar and the hunger bar. I’m not quite sure why there’s a need for the hunger bar at all, consider that this game isn’t a survival game that heavily relies on staying hydrated or being healthy, but since it got me to get rid of most of the consumables stocked within my inventory in order to not starve, I guess that will do.
TAoT included some RPG elements within Formagetus and most often than not, you’ll find yourself grinding for materials needed for quests, or simply gathering EXP to level up. The game also offers an unforgiving game world filled with hostile monsters roaming about and has proved to be quite easy to die very early on in the game. On a side note, it is wise to put a good use in the chests located within and outside of your home, because once you’ve died, there’s a chance that you will drop important materials within your inventory. If you want to retrieve your items, you might have to walk back to where you’ve died after fighting off whatever monster that killed you earlier.
In any case, the game doesn’t have top notched graphics or a complicated battle system with skill tree or whatnot, but it is simply a small gem for you to discover and experience on a Sunday afternoon. I really enjoyed playing this game, waving a hatchet around as a lavender Tree with a creepy smile and I definitely recommend this game for those that are interested in trying it out.

The Adventures of Tree is side-scroller, open world, action adventure, where you play as … well, a tree. I play the game for almost 7 h and this is my first impressions.
For a 2D game it have a lot of settings. In the graphics section there are Resolution, Subtitles, Motion Blur, V-sync, Fullscreen and Depth of Field. The game runs smoothly with 60 FPS and you can even play it on Windows XP. Audio options are plenty. There six different sliders – ambient, movie, mob, GUI, music and others. Excelent work! There is full controller support and you can rebind the keys, even for the controller. I didn't try how is the gameplay with him, but I think it's the preferable to play with a controller.
