Just to clarify, this game is in pre-Alpha. Not Alpha. Not Beta. Not even a conventional state of "early access".
As the disclaimer at the start of the game says, it represents the absolute core mechanics of the game, and doesn't even have a title screen or save-game functionality.
That being said, it's actually pretty good. Though all of the mechanics are barebones and not particularly tied together at this stage (for example, click a room, hire a chemist, he'll show up at your Main District but won't automatically go to work in that room), but it's a good concept and a very good start.
A word of warning though: This is not a base builder game. It is not an RTS game. It is not open world. It is not Evil Genius or Prison Architect. It is very much a resource management game. You have limited space, limited vans, limited expansion locations. Everything costs something, and when you lose that thing, you have to pay (or fight) to get it back.
From what the devs have been saying, it looks like the final game will veer a little closer to being a base builder, but more in the XCOM: Enemy Unknown style.
Which is actually a pretty accurate summation, as it stands: It's XCOM for drugs.
This game's more addictive than the drugs you make in it! (It's just like Breaking Bad)

Wow, this game almost sent me to sleep! If I wasn't such a perfectionist, I wouldn't have bothered playing the whole thing through.
Warning, contains some *spoilers*, although the 'thrilling' nature of the story doesn't really require spoiling
The negatives:
- It's so banal as to be unreal! I don't care about the protagonist, I don't care about the love interest, I don't care about the stupid town.
- The story is unbelievable and insulting. So, I've lost my memory and yet after rescuing a man I haven't seen for 10 years I still want to work together with him to rebuild the town I left? I haven't got a job or a life or anything since then? The whole story revolves about the fact that the female protagonist was being fought over by two men, one of whom was an evil genius and she never even thinks to raise this as an objection?
- The puzzles are so simple that all fun has been squeezed out of the game. So much relies on me finding an object in a scene and the place it belongs being highlighted almost immediately so I'm just a point, click, drop grunt for most of the game. The only pay off being able to watch an animation? Some of the puzzles you just click through by trial and error rather than stretching any sort of brain you might have left.
- Why, oh why is there an orange dog as my hint???? Is it because being female, my character can only interact with children's toys? Perhaps it's because I skipped the tutorial, perhaps the startling plot revelations about this plastic monstrosity were filled in during some epic plot-twist. Or perhaps it's because the developers think all women like children's toys, marriage and puppies.
The positives:
- It looks nice in a cutesy, twee sort of way. And they must have spent some time on it.
- It gave me a break from shooting zombies / created a calm space after playing the horrors of 'I have no mouth and I must scream' which may require a lifetime of therapy to recover from.
- It's so easy, I'll probably be able to play it after a lobotomy.
- If you're a concerned parent who just wants an almost completely harmless (gender stereotypes aside) game for your 6-9 year old to play, then it's probably ok on sale.

The Baconing is an isometric action game with very minor RPG elements. The graphical style of the game is somewhat unique. Many background objects look like props in a play and the game overall has a bit of a cartoonish look. The world is a bit weird and it looks like you're moving on roller, because the land is always crooked.
The gameplay is very combat heavy, but the combat isn't that much fun. You die quite fast on the harder difficulties and you have to block a lot. You can also reflect projectiles the enemies shoot at you with the shield, but you have to time it right. You have 2 weapon sets and you can quickly switch between them anytime you want. Each weapon set has two weapons that you can choose yourself. I used the other weapon set for normal weapons and the other one for Justice weapons. Justice weapons have a powerful special attack, which can be used when you fill your Justice bar by hitting enemies and blocking at the right time. The game also has a local co-op so you can play with a friend. One player is always playing as Deathspank, but the other player can choose one character out of 4 (5 if you have the DLC).
The few RPG elements the game has consist of collecting gear and leveling up and then choosing a hero card that boosts damage, health or some other thing. The levels mainly enable you to wear better gear and that's pretty much it. The gear system is pretty stupid, because you almost always get a better gear set when you go to a new area and then the old gear set becomes useless. Same goes for weapons and few consumables.
The game has an economy system, which doesn't really make sense. You get money from enemies and also by grinding your useless items and the only thing worth buying with the money is more consumables, because the weapon vendor only sells you items you've previously had. I only had to buy a few potions during my playthrough, so I had lots of money that I had no use for.
The strongest part of the game and the reason I liked the game, despite all its problems, is the humor and dialogue. The characters are quite funny and a lot of the dialogue consists of silliness. There are lots of somewhat random moments as well like en. So if you like that kind of humor and don't mind the somewhat dull combat, I recommend playing the game. The combat isn't that bad, if you have a friend to play with.

This game, although charming, not too easy, and all in all create a pretty enjoyable expierence; the gameplay and the repetitiveness of all of the quests get pretty boring pretty quick. I havent tried DeathSpank or the sequal to that yet, but I imagine they are more fun than this one.      4.5/10

I grew up playing Sonic games, first in the sega genesis(Sonic 1, 2, and 3&Knuckles) and then the gamecube(Sonic Adventure 1 and 2, Heroes, and  Shadow). So while I haven't played any of the more modern Sonic games for systems like the Xbox360 and such, I am still familiar with the classic 2D and the first 3D games.
Now, a game that combines the basic 2D sonic and the more dynamic 3D sounds pretty good also because it gives you a chance to revisit zones from past Sonic games, but now with beautiful graphics. The more I play, the more I realise I no longer need this spongy human form keeping me tethered to this mortal plane. The "graphical glitches" that make it seem as though there are unexplored areas to my side are in reality the game trying to confuse my sense of direction further; the "mouse lock" I keep feeling is simply me falling unconscious briefly; and the repetition of button presses to make part of the UI work are just me perceiving time in a whole new way. I only pressed it once, but it felt like a thousand times.
Though it would appear I've only played half an hour of this game, I assure you it was longer. This game has changed my physiology for the better, and I finally feel as though I am who I was born to be, for the first time.

Quick review after a few hours of play, from a fan of this genre of games:
- windowed mode is bugged and causes black screen, can't close window, has to kill process
- full screen has black borders on left/right and you can't alt-tab to other processes, like a web browser
- game crashes when clicking on portraits ( edit: already fixed, requires reinstall )
- user interface is old-school in the bad way: requires lots of extra clicks. Expect insane clicking even for basic functionality.
- to speed up combat you need to click the rounds, so for trash encounters you end up clicking like a madman ( edit: you can speed up by using enter, didn't know that due to lack of manual. Helps quite a bit ).
- game is pretty difficult/old-school. Expect to have to remake your party due to getting blocked in game due to not having the right skills/spells to progress.
On the positive side, I'm having fun and I can see how a fan of this kind of game will enjoy it ( expect your share of treasures, secrets, loot, random combat and even talkable NPCs via a keyword system ). For others, be aware that this game is not for the weak and requires thinking.
For a game 20-years in development and delayed so many times, I'm kindda disapointed by the amount of bugs and technical issues. Therefore I cannot recommend the game at the moment but once everything gets fixed/patched, it'd become a good niche game.
In summary, you'll like this game on the following conditions:
- fan of turn-based blobbers
- can withstand technical issues, bugs and difficulty
- can withstand a UI and graphics that are obsolete and requires lots of clicking
- don't mind the $40 price
If you do not satisfy those conditions, I would recommend to do a lot of research before buying this game.

I couldnt decide what to write in this review , so im gonna share with you guys my favorite apple pie recipe Enjoy! :
Pastry
2 cups all-purpose flour
1 teaspoon salt
2/3 cup plus 2 tablespoons shortening
4 to 6 tablespoons cold water
Filling
1/3 to 1/2 cup sugar
1/4 cup all-purpose flour
1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
1/2 teaspoon ground nutmeg
1/8 teaspoon salt
8 cups thinly sliced peeled tart apples (8 medium)
2 tablespoons butter or margarine
1) In medium bowl, mix 2 cups flour and 1 teaspoon salt. Cut in shortening, using pastry blender (or pulling 2 table knives through ingredients in opposite directions), until particles are size of small peas. Sprinkle with cold water, 1 tablespoon at a time, tossing with fork until all flour is moistened and pastry almost cleans side of bowl (1 to 2 teaspoons more water can be added if necessary).
2) Gather pastry into a ball. Divide in half; shape into 2 flattened rounds on lightly floured surface. Wrap in plastic wrap; refrigerate about 45 minutes or until dough is firm and cold, yet pliable. This allows the shortening to become slightly firm, which helps make the baked pastry more flaky. If refrigerated longer, let pastry soften slightly before rolling.
3) Heat oven to 425°F. With floured rolling pin, roll one pastry round into round 2 inches larger than upside-down 9-inch glass pie plate. Fold pastry into fourths; place in pie plate. Unfold and ease into plate, pressing firmly against bottom and side.
4) In large bowl, mix sugar, 1/4 cup flour, the cinnamon, nutmeg and 1/8 teaspoon salt. Stir in apples until well mixed. Spoon into pastry-lined pie plate. Cut butter into small pieces; sprinkle over filling. Trim overhanging edge of pastry 1/2 inch from rim of plate.
5) Roll other round of pastry into 10-inch round. Fold into fourths and cut slits so steam can escape. Unfold top pastry over filling; trim overhanging edge 1 inch from rim of plate. Fold and roll top edge under lower edge, pressing on rim to seal; flute as desired. Cover edge with 2- to 3-inch strip of foil to prevent excessive browning.
6) Bake 40 to 50 minutes or until crust is brown and juice begins to bubble through slits in crust, removing foil for last 15 minutes of baking. Serve warm if desired.
Enjoy!

text:
TLDR:
If you usually like to understand games and if you have even the patience that you usually need on PURE RPG games well you will love the "almost" infinite crafting possibilities you will find in this game, and this game will be so easy to play that you will ask yourself "Am I really playing at the hardest difficulty?". If you don't have those two qualities don't buy this game; you will totally miss the fun and this game will become IMPOSSIBLE to play and you will ask yourself "Why I'm not able to wounding my enemies?"
LV:
I was just looking for my girlfriend (if you choose the male)/my sister (if you choose the woman) and I've discovered that I am one of the most powerful mages in the whole planet so I said to myself: "let's go out there and save the entire world".
Let's be clear: this game is the typical LOVE it or HATE it. What the developers tried to do here is something of unique barely seen in other games but this created a huge mess for the typical "I want to launch my game and just have fun" players.
First of all crafting is not that clear, you have to read you have to mess a bit with it, you have to try, you have to destroy and craft again and so on. Because if a spell is at Tier 9 it doesn't mean it could do more damage than a spell at Tier 7 due to perks and bonuses. You have to be careful about what to do and again you have to READ what you are crafting.
And even the most useless (at the first sight) spell could be DEVASTATING USEFULL. For example my shield is not that strong (only almost 3000hp per pip still at tier 9 tho) but it gives me the bonus of unlimited blink. This is a huge advantage if you usually move a lot to avoid people shooting at you. My delirium spell (at the first it seems useless but I had to take a step backward about it) gives me a bonus of a x2-x11 crit multiplier that means after launching that if I shoot at the target I can instantly kill it (even bosses with 3-5 shoots!). And so on.
About this you can use the smart inventory that will automatically update your spells. But remember sometimes smart inventory could give you great ideas, sometime doing things by yourself is BETTER.
So yes it is a game that you have to understand and that you have to adapt to your gameplay style because IT DOESN'T adapt to you.
So again is not for everyone.
Second, the graphic is indeed amazing (well...CryEngine 3 you know...) the sounds are good and even the music it is. The scenarios will leave you with your mouth open. If you have a middle range nVidia card BEWARE because this game was made with AMD support so you could have some trouble and it doesn't depends from your GPU but from the software itself so you may have to tweak it a bit (no problem with my 970 anyway)
Third, the story leaves you a bit unsatisfied; yes it engages you at a certain point but it leaves a lot of doors open in the end (probably the developers were thinking about a Lichdom 2 who knows and personally I hope for it). At the end of the game starts the "New gameb" mode. You will be able to teleport yourself in every area of the game, plus there will be new portals to explore (and to let you maximize your spells by unlocking tier 10 and above)
The gameplay in general is quite linear, go ahead, devastate everything you see, go ahead, find some loot machines to clear,  fight the boss start the next level. Simple and linear, no puzzle and not a lot of exploration.
What I think about it?
This game has got a lot of potential, but is not for the taste of everyone. As we all well know pretty graphics don't make a game good, gameplay and story does.
So again, if you like to craft and experiment a lot go ahead buy this game; or if you are willing to try it because you are curious buy it when it is on sales.
If you want a game with a deep intense story and without a 100% guaranteed headache due to crafting DON'T buy this game.
Overall
Graphic 9/10
Sounds 8/10
Gameplay 7/10
Longevity 7/10
Controls 7/10

I guess I'll write a review for this game. Where to start? I guess I'll start at
The story:
You play as a member of the 501st legion, the personal clone army for the Chancellor. The events start towards the end of Episode 3, right before order 66 is executed. It then shows the transition from Clone trooper to Stormtrooper. It's an excellent journey, and it helps mesh the two movies together in a way not seen before.
Galactic Conquest:
When I first got this game back in 2005 on the PS2, I didn't really care much for galactic conquest. After buying it on steam and giving it a shot, it's by far the most addicting mode in the game. Essentially there are 4 versions of this mode. One where you play as the rebellion trying to stop the Empire once and for all, one where you play as the Empire, trying to crush the rebellion, one where you play as the Republic trying to assert dominance over the galaxy and restore peace, and one where you play as the CIS trying to control thr trade routes of the entire galaxy. Whatever you choose, the core gameplay is more or less the same. You start by controlling a few planets and taking turns either attacking a planet or defending you planet. The enemy can build a fleet on any planet they control, and can attack your ships even if they aren't next to a planet, engaging in large space battles. Whether you're fighting on the ground or in space, it's a hell of a lot of fun.
And finally,
Instant Action:
Are you sick of having to go through the campaign to get into battles? Do you wish you could get into a battle in seconds? Well now you can! With modes such as 2-flag assualt, conquest, and assualt (best mode), you have plenty of options. There are also options for space battles. Do you want to instantly fight for the airspace over Kashyyyk? now you can! Do you want to fight on the ground over the clone-producing factories of Kamino? Now you can! In all seriousness, it's a great mode, and one that I wish more games nowadays would incorporate.
Final Verdict:
This game is simply amazing. Star Wars fans can argue over which movie is the greatest all day, but there's no arguing that this is the most creative and immersive Star Wars experience in a game. With all the options and modes, there's no shortage of things to do, unlike another certain battlefront game. It is worth every penny. With the new addition of the previously shut down online servers, it's truly worth picking back up.
Overall, with the amazing immersiveness and continued support of the online mode by Steam servers, I will give this game a near-perfect 96/100. There are flaws with the online mode such as connecting to servers, but the amazing single player modes outweigh the problems of the small online modes. If you want a true Star Wars experience, buy this. You won't regret it.

The Baconing is a simple and short action RPG with a humorous setting and plot. The settings are mostly interesting and they change at a decent pace. Humour is derived from decently written dialoque as well as absurd enviroments, items and creatures. Main gameplay revolves around killing numerous amounts of baddies.
Though the visual aesthetic is generally appealing, the simple gameplay gets really repetitive quick. Unfortunately, same goes for the humour. RPG's are really good targets for parody, but it seems like the Baconing misses the point on occasion and when it hits the target, it doesn't quite have the right delivery. The voice acting of the main character gets really grating by the end, even though the game isn't that long.
On top of that, the Baconing was clearly made for a controller in mind. Though playing with mouse and keyboard is serviceable, it is occasionally clunky and can get annoying in big group fights.

The storyline to the Baconing IS funny. What isn't is the "local co-op". Something that doesn't really appear on all those trailers touting the extra playable characters and sidekicks to the main character. What makes it worse is the amount of searching you have to do just to get a straight answer as to what EXACTLY "local co-op" means for a game whose amuzing storyline and colourful, action-packed gameplay makes it seem like the perfect game to play with a friend....
What it means is, should you buy this game on Steam with plans for a co-op playthrough, your friend will either have to (somehow) share the keyboard with you OR (more likely) bring a console controller along to plug in.
Yes, that's right, after the fans of previous games clamouring for a better multiplayer option that could only have increased sales, the company have allowed this game to become little more than another trouble port, while not making it clear from the get-go that one of the game's main selling points is severely limited.
Unless you are looking for that info specifically while researching the game-- and even then --you will likely not realise this suspiciously brushed-under-the-table piece of info and will likely purchase the game before realising the issue. A shame really, since all it serves to do is remind PC gamers that the game is JUST a port, and harms future sales of what can easily be a fun experience, as many gamers have and will continue to swear off any of the developer's future products.
In reality, it only shows how that last little bit of effort to really make the game great was either too much effort for the developer or something they saw as not worth investing in, for their customers. As I said, a shame for a product that otherwise could have been easily recommendable.

It's sad as I was really looking forward to this game, but it's just not fun to play, and it was ruined simply due to a few major factors that killed the game for me (note that I only play RTSs in singleplayer).
The first problem that is it SHOULD have built upon Stronghold 2, which was an excellent game that was killed by a handful of crippling flaws (random crippling gong/rat disasters, resources were too demanding for basic units, and bad mission/campaign structures and progression. Instead this time they overcautiously regressed to Stronghold 1, but kept a lot of SH2 flaws and included a bunch of new ones.
The engine is actually less advanced than its predecessor in many ways that hurts the gameplay. Firstly, it is very buggy: dying enemies spawn giant triangles that block the screen, and in one mission my keep was invisible.
The interface is horrible- unlike the previous games that allowed very simple, versatile and accurate structure placement, this version seems incomplete- placing structures is clumsy, fiddly and difficult, walls are much harder to place OR connect (especially to structures that are supposed to back onto them like the Barracks), and the AI is awful, where the player often loses control for extended periods by sending units onto battlements. Combat is also a pain to organize
The multi-storey defenses are GONE with plain Strong-hold 1 structures returning (a pity). Yet the gameplay elements that turned Stronghold 2 from excellent to downright bad ARE STILL HERE. Random unpreventable disasters are back (which at least are more managable and less crippling than last time- except for the bears that spawn inside my castle and wipe out my farms). The awful campaign/mission structure in the previous game is back, with annoying and frustrating missions like escorting VERY slow units around, with the first proper defensive mission not occurring until the FOURTH LEVEL (the first mission archers are available too- before then you get your peasants to charge the enemy). Also, while the goofy characters and dialogue from Stronghold 2 are gone, there is simply no characters or dialogue at all- you get a few still-frame comics with a narrated monologue voiceover (by the Wolf and the two heroes only) at the start and end of each mission, and that's it.  One very good positive over the last game however is that lower units like archers no longer require Honour (which was a good idea- but should have only applied to top-level units to make them harder to spam).
Overall it's a huge pity, as Firefly had a lot to work with by their previous games, and could have very easily made an excellent game. Instead it feels rushed and incomplete, with far less sophistication than the previous game, and worse, little evidence that the team did much engine testing or gameplay testing before shipping it out.
I do genuinely hope they give it another shot, because they DO have the capability to make their next game amazing.

So, a few months ago, I think Bundlestars snuck this in with the Apogee Retro Pack for like $5 and I couldn't resist. Overall, that pack had 40 games in it, including Halloween Harry and all the pre-DNF PC Duke Nukem Games. That was enough nostalgia to get me to bite, and so I wound up with this in my inventory.
I'm trying to figure out a way not to be mean to this game. I really, really, am. But see, I played 40 minutes of this right now and something about it made me feel irritated enough to the point where I actually got a little physically ill.
That, for me, is a very strange reaction to have towards anything, let alone a game. I think I can explain how this happened, though.
In order for an FPS about being a hardcore awesome mage to work, you need a few things.
1) Spells should have an obvious visceral impact.
2) Controls should respond to the slightest movement.
3) Menus and interfaces should be intuitive enough to ensure you're rarely out of the action.
Lichdom: Battlemage, for me, achieved none of those things.
Instead, what I got was a game that very badly wanted to be both an exciting nonstop action mage FPS, but also a reasonably complex RPG with deep crafting elements. Lichdom seems to have succeeded somewhat in being a Frankengame because it happens to end up with the worst elements of a shooter, and an RPG.
The game gives up on explaining its own menus pretty quickly, leaving you to figure a good amount of the game out, and the controls feel somehow like you're always acting on some serious input delay.
Part of me feels bad for not carrying on and giving the game a fairer shake, but I simply cannot enjoy a shooter in which launching a fireball takes a noticeable delay after I click, and has all the impact of a feather duster when it actually reaches its target. Enemies simply POOF out of existence with a little puff of smoke. Physics attached to enemy gibs could have really made all the difference here, but the system as-is feels somehow weak. For a supposedly tough-as-nails mage, I was left wondering why it felt as though my spells merely tickled my opposition until the game decided to replace them with a "dead pile of bones" texture on the ground.
The more I type, the more I'm reminded of that feeling in the pit of my stomach. Lichdom has a lot of great ideas, and that makes it all the more upsetting. It looks nice, but it's static. It aims to revitalize Hexen, but it fails to feel fast or responsive. It tries to tell a mystical story, but its voice acting and writing is all over the place.
These disappointments, and others like them, leave me with this uneffable sensation that enough is enough, and 40 minutes is all I can take. I simply can't get into this. Lichdom has the best of intentions, but intentions and ability to follow through are very, very different things.

The basic concept is as follows:
You're a prospect and your goal is to fight the boss at the end of the game. To do this you have to defeat 7 minibosses throughout the game, each in different areas. There are many enemies along the way that will try to stop you and you will have to defeat them gaining new items and leveling up as you go.
The main draw towards this game is the multiplayer, you are in a world with many other actual players and you can each do your own thing. You can however request a party with others (up to 3) and fight minibosses and enemies together. The only other way of communicating is via the emote system in-game as there is no voice or text chat implemented. If you want you can simply attack others and this yields interesting results.
The leveling system is a point based system where each level will gain you a point, there are 6 different slots for your points to go into and each give their respected benefit.
You will pick up loot from enemies you kill, chests and from killing other players.
It takes a very minimalist approach to a fighting game. It's alot like Dark Souls in the sense there's no map, the story is very obsure and it doesn't tell you alot. However it's a very fun game and I definetely recommend it.

I may have recommended this game, doesnt mean it is perfect. It needs alot of improvement. It's not difficult, it uses cheap tactics like overwhelming you with enemies.

Absolver is a great game, but do not purchase it with the wrong ideas.
Absolver has minimal story, and what can count as it's campaign is more or less a long tutorial, to show you all of the zones, understand basic attacks, and gain your usable abilities and such.
The game's purpose, and where it shines, is in it's PvP aspects. Right now there is currently only 1v1, but soon there will be 3v3 and ranked battles as well. The game's combat is based off of creating combos with a set of pre-learned moves, and discovering more through blocking and countering enemy moves. Revisiting areas is to gain new moves and armor as you prepare yourself and unlock new movesets for PvP fun.
This game is great, but don't go into it expecting a story. Buy Absolver if you want an interesting take on an online 3d brawler.
Do note the game is region locked, and you will not be able to play with friends overseas. While they may unlock regions in the future, know of this lock before buying.

It's hard to decide whether to recommend this game or not. I paid £25 for the game, which based on the trailers etc seemed perfectly reasonable. However with a grand total of 4 hours gametime at the point of writing this review, I have completed the "story" so to speak. I have defeated all the bosses in the game.
There is no new content or areas for me from this point. However that being said, I can PvP until my hearts content. I shall break down my experience into some pros and cons.
PROS:
-Design. Gorgeous world, albeit very simplistic, but it looks okay and doesn't detract from the complexity of the combat.
-The combat. Is great, and requires genuine practice and skill to be successful.
-Multiplayer. While it lasted, it was fun to randomly come across other people and either help them or decide to fight them for a laugh.
CONS:
-Length. As stated, completed the "story" in around 3 hours of actual play time.
-You can literally run past all enemies except the bosses with little difficulty (???).
-Drive. There is almost zero explanation for your being in the world, why you're fighting the people you do fight etc. There is no argument to be made for Dark Souls style story telling, as there is almost no dialogue and the item descriptions don't say anything significant. There isn't a story to this game.
-Confusion. You get told to fight 3 bosses and 6 hard enemies. That is literally the entirety of the game. All you get is a "map" if you can call it that with lights on it, that go out when you defeat your foes.
-The world is actually tiny. If you don't stop to fight enemies, which you don't have to do, you could probably run a circuit around it in about 5-10 minutes if that.
- OH MY GOD THE LAG. If just one guy in your vicinity has a poor connection, EVERYONE nearby takes rubberbanding to an extreme level. Honestly terribly thought out net code for now, hopefully this will be fixed. (If everyone has a decent connection online functionality is fine), this is the internet, SOMEONE WILL have a bad connection. It's incredibly frustrating trying to fight the AI and lagging cos some guy just appeared in your area with 1000ms ping.
-Another lag issue: in the supposedly competetive 1v1 fights, if your opponent is laggy, YOU will get punished for it. Too many times my enemy has appeared to stand still and then I've rubber banded off the edge of the map. Completely unfair for now, this had better get fixed.
-Every enemy is the same. Every grunt enemy has the same AI, just slight variations in movesets but honestly you can get through the game the moves you start off given, and not really change your playstyle to adapt to your enemies. ALL the bosses are just the same as you, again with slightly different movesets and varied aggression (the last boss is the same as the others but seems to attack faster).
It's hard to put my finger on how I feel about this game. While playing it I had a great time, albeit a bit of a confused one. However when I killed the third boss I genuinely though huh I guess I have to find a new path somewhere. It seemed to be the end of a first act. Nope, end of the game, all you get for finishing the game is a fancy cloak that EVERYONE will have in a couple days time.
I guess if you LOVE multiplayer fighting this game would totally be for you, but if you want a complex world to explore it's certainly not worth £25 of your money. That said, I'm recommending it because I had fun while it lasted and I'm told more will be added (again though, not sure if that's new areas to explore or just new combat styles). I wouldn't put too much faith in that promise, as many studios have said such things in the past and failed to deliver.
EDIT** am going to not recommend until the lag issues are fixed, having played a couple more days of the game, lag literally kills the 1v1 fights, it's not fun at all to get beaten by someone teleporting around the arena.
Be warned. All the screenshots and videos are from PhotoDirector 8 Ultra

How have I never reviewed this game? Buy it. It's the best. Even for a game from 2010, the graphics look pretty good. The sun beating off the snow covered ground still looks exceptional. There is honestly no other game I've ever played that captures 1940's post war like the first couple chapters in this game. The snow, the cars, the map, etc. Even the way the cars drive - there are actually a couple second between shifts as automatic transmissions weren't a thing yet. When the story shifts to the 1950's, you can drive the Cadillac Series 62, one of the first production cars to have an automatic in real life, and, sure enough, it shifts like an automatic in game. That attention to detail is everything to me - especially being a car guy. But, more than anything, I'm a history guy. History is mah sh*t. It makes me wet. This game made me feel like I just got home from the war and joined the Mafia. You won't regret buying it... unless you're an a**hole. Put the driving settings on "simulation." It's so much better. I rarely speed in this game. It's so emersive that I don't mind actually going the speed limit. I've played through the campaign five or six times. I really love this game that much. So, again, purchase it. If you don't enjoy it, I'll give you twenty bucks. Not really... go f*ck yourself.

Blehh... I don't want to review this.
Why? Because my opinion is quite mixed. On the one hand, the story is competent and kept me interested in the game (though the ending was sudden and unsatisfying). On the other, the gameplay was somewhat mediocre due to its dependence upon cover-based shooting. Also, while it is a "sandbox" game, there isn't actually much to do in the open world. Really, this game is all about its story missions. Why the open world even exists... I don't know. They don't even let you mess around in it after you finish the story like most games of this sort do.
I loved Mafia 1, but that was many years ago. Chances are if I played that again I'd be a bit more negative since that game also had an open world with basically nothing to do in it. Mafia 2, essentially, is Mafia 1 but with a weaker story and nude collectibles. And since I don't care about the latter... ultimately this game was a bit disappointing since my expectations were so high.
Still, this isn't a bad game. I've given "yes" votes to much worse games than this. Still, I would give this a "maybe" if I could. If you are interested in a story-driven game in the world of organized crime, then this is probably something to check out. You may like it. :o
Just... don't go in hoping for sandbox funtimes, because you are not really going to find them here.

This is a fairly short HOPA game; I finished it in slightly less than 3 hrs.  Unlike many other HOPA games there aren't any typical HOPA scenes.  Instead almost every location is a bit of a HOPA puzzle where you have to find items and place them in the world to remove obstacles.  The upshot is that instead of finding objects which have nothing to do with the story, which you usually do in this genre, you are constantly finding objects which are directly tied to solving obstacles.
The art work was good enough and the animations are about what you'd expect from the genre.  The only major criticism I have is the cartoon dog who gives you hints.  You can see him in the screen shots above.  He is constantly moving the entire game in a fairly fast and jerky animation.  It's not a subtle movement at all.  I found it completely distracting; so much so that I put a tissue box over that part of my monitor to block him out.  I though the dog was a truly terrible part to an otherwise fine, but short, HOPA game.

True, the story was disjointed.
True, the puzzles were a bit simplistic.
True, the objects weren't exactly hidden.
But the reason I cannot recommend this game is that freakin' robotic hint seizure-dog wouldn't stop convulsing the entire freakin' time I played. That dog should come with its own epilepsy warning. And I used to think that Windows XP search dog was annoying ... the seizure-dog takes annoying to a whole new level.

I actually regret the spare change I spent on this bit of silliness. The ridiculously convoluted story was was a bit more asinine than the problem solving which included strange leaps of logic like "use the carousel to move that pile of junk." The hints in the game were generally useless, leaving me to hunt around the screen for things to click randomly and hope that something would start to make sense soon. The only thing that kept me going was my own stubborness and a sort of sick fascination with what the writers were possibly going to do to resolve everything.
Don't waste your spare change on this. Buy a cup of coffee, instead.

There is a mod for FTL called Captain's Edition.  I have played much more of it with that mod than without it, so my review may or may not be accurate for the vanilla experience.
There's a reason you see "Overwhelmingly Positive" at the top by the scores.  FTL is simply amazing.  It's well done, insanely difficult without being impossible, and random enough to not become dull over time.  The pacing is fantastic because you control it.  Since you can pause and unpause as you see fit, and direct your shots and crew while paused, even gamers who aren't used to rapid action can make the most of the tactical experience the game has to offer.
Pros: Lots of weapons and crew types mean you can customize your style.  Like to engage in melee and capture ships whole?  Teleporters!  Like to strategically time your volley to pass through the enemy shields? Ion weapons make the shields fizzle wonderfully.  Don't like making your crew run to the medbay when they have a boo-boo?  Put in a clone-bay instead and let them die on the job!
Cons: The final boss represents a giant leap in difficulty that may seem unfair the first few hundred times you get there.  Sometimes the RNG is a cruel mistress as well.

WARNING! This game contains a decent level of animated gore and voilence. Recommended age: 15+
Introduction:
Iron Snout is a game where you play as an adventurous little pig, let astray from his family, and trying his best to get back home. Although the high level or gore and voilence may be unexpected, Iron Snout is a heart-warming adventure game that pulls you in, and makes you lust for more of this beautiful game.
Review:
The graphics are on-par with that of many modern-day AAA games, such as Nekopara Vol. 3, and the lore is one that no-one will want to stop reading. The combat is another unbelievably amazing experience, with in-depth fight scenes that can last between 1 minute and 2 hours of intense button mashing. Lastly, the multitude of gamemodes is what truly enhances the gameplay of Iron Snout, exposing the true story of the little pig, and all throughout pulling you in even more.
Verdict:
I, unfortunately, have not been able to play Iron Snout as much as I have wanted to, yet of all the games I have played, it is the only one that I can see myself coming back to in the future, time and time again, as I have already done in the past few years.
With the conclusion of:
- amazing graphics;
- teary-eyed lore;
- ground breaking combat;
I give Iron Snout a solid 10/10 'oinks'. May the Snout live on for another day! :)

Bloody Good Time is a first person shooter that takes a new and irreverent approach to multiplayer mayhem by putting players on a Hollywood set, where they get to choose their thrill.
From a spring-break beach house, to a hotel, players will discover the merciless world of movie studios where anyone can star in a Hollywood blockbuster film as long as they are willing to kill for the role.
The game is set up for a max of eight players online or via LAN play, giving it a multiplayer experience like no other.
In the game, players can be as devious or ruthless as possible by killing other competitors in nasty and brutal ways. Players can use an arsenal of toon-esque weapons including guns, a frying pan and even an exploding remote-controlled rat to throw the movie set into true mayhem and chaos.
Players will be able to choose from a variety of stereotypical B-movie characters, such as the bikini beach babe, the creepy clown, the reject ninja girl or the super jock. Each character is unique enough to not feel as if they are all clones of each other.
During gameplay, the players are tasked with killing their "prey" without getting caught by the security team.
This can be accomplished by multiple means...
Ever wanted to ambush someone while they were on the toilet? Well, you can do that!  Using a chainsaw perhaps?
In fact, the game encourages you to be as devious and under handed as you can possibly be.
The art style is very close to another game in the same genre named "Spy vs Spy" except here, the style is more anime based.
The beach babes and reject ninja girls are beautifully animated, with amazingly funny boob physics and a number of other amusing antics.
Bloody Good Time is very cartoony without being super unrealistic, similar to how Team Fortress 2's art style works.  It just adds to the fun of the gameplay.
Sound plays less of a roll than in other games of the genre.
Apart from the announcer who comes in the form of a movie director, nothing really stands out, apart from the satisfying clang of a frying pan connecting with someone’s head in a dark corner of the movie set…
All of the guns have unique sounds and you can easily locate a firefight just by audio queues.
Firing a gun can be dangerous as it gives your position away and indicates that there are no security members around. From there, its war!
Bloody Good Time is… well… a bloody good time with its cartoony art style, unique concept, unique characters and a bucket of humour thrown in for good measure.
It has all the makings of an awesome party game and is a must play with friends.
Unfortunately, multiplayer is semi dead as of this review, but I hope a sequel comes out one day.
This is a must buy for people who enjoy the “Murder” game mode found in Garry’s Mod, as it is very similar with unique characters with their own reasons for wanting the role.

I'm sure many people will request someone judge this game based on Grand Theft Auto or a similar game.  However that's a mistake.  Mafia 2 is NOT a GTA game, while yes there's a world, and you can explore the game as you want at times, this is an extremely linear story, with only one part of the game (A scant ten minutes) which gives you an open ended task.   That's 10 minutes of an almost 15 hour game.
A quick note: I was not a fan of the original Mafia.  However I was curious about the desire for Mafia 3 so I tried this game out.
That's not to say someone can't compare them, but the point is this is a VERY story driven game.  If you're not a fan of Mafia movies, you're probably going to dislike this game.  Not only is it heavily based on the same subject, but much of the game is similar to those movies.  That's not to say they stole from the movies or anything, but as I played I noticed a number of scenes that feel lifted from Godfather.  Hell you have a guy named Vito making his way up.
Then again this story isn't like even GTA Vice City, where the entire game is just a retelling of Scarface, instead there's a very solid and good story that involves a number of interesting characters, and honestly, while you might have an idea where the end of the game is (seriously, mafia stories end only two ways).  The game delivers it's story well.
There's no open world component here, even at the end of the game, there's no true free roam.  As I said there's 10 minutes of free roam when you need to make a little money.  But the majority of the game allows you to explore the city and see everything but there's nothing to do besides the next mission.  It's a lovely vibrant city and it's not a huge fault, but if someone's looking for a ton of stuff to do, this isn't the game.  If someone instead wants a solid narrative and a story that drives the player forward, well Mafia 2 does that.
I kept playing because I wanted to see the end of the game, and when I was done, I thought I enjoyed it.  I'd give this game a 4 stars.  That other star.  Well let's get into some negatives.
First off I found one almost game breaking bug, in chapter 12, apparently entering a building through one door instead of the other broke the script and that's a pretty major bug, I was ready to give up through frustration before someone mentioned a fix in a thread I read.  A fix from 4 years ago!   Come on 2k!.
Second we need to talk about collectibles.  Let's first talk about the bad.  There's wanted posters, and a few of them are near impossible to collect.  And there's 159 of them!! Come on!   Not only is there too many, but collectibles shouldn't be impossible to get.
On the other hand, there's another collectible.  As you play through the story, there's chapters and each chapter has 2-4 playboys.  Yes Playboys, you collect the magazine and get a pin up picture.  And um, yeah they're old classic pin up photos.   To put it simply, it's odd.  I mean in a game that has no nudity, even when a character showers, or when there's numerous girls around, there's just porn in the collectibles.  WTF?   I'm not complaining mind you, it's just a very odd choice.    Though making it so you have to collect them as you play through the story was a good design choice in my opinion, it meant you would go near them (For the most part) and have to collect them then, as if you try to grab one in an area you can get to in the wrong chapter, it wouldn't be there.
The gameplay is solid, I've heard people rag about the gunplay, but it's quite good.  The difficulty of the game is pretty easy, up til the final chapters, where hard gets ridiculously hard, but medium is almost never a challenge.   There's even an option to turn on simulation driving, that did make the car control more realistically.  A great addition but I turned it off after a while.  It really is nice, but why add difficulty in evading police?
And finally let's talk about the music.  I love it, this game has everything, old Italian standards, doo wop, and as the story is told over two decades the music changes with the time.  It's a brilliant use of music to push the story forward.
Now I got this game in a humble bundle, I should mention that, but this game made me excited about Mafia 3.  When Mafia 3 comes out, I'll be watching because if it can deliver a game, and a story like this one.  I won't really have a problem paying for it.    As I mentioned earlier, I didn't like Mafia 1 that much, Mafia 2 is a complete 180, I really enjoyed this game.  I wouldn't call it love, and I wish people were more upfront about it not being a sandbox/open world game, but besides that, it's a fantastic game, and was well worth the 15 or so hours I put into the main story.
Strong recommend.

After playing Mafia 2 to completion i can honestly say that it is as paper thin as the first game. I'm going to write a short list of pros and cons that will hopefully detail my thoughts on the game.
Pros
-Atmosphere
- The games 40s/50s setting is just amazing to see, i absolutely love the time its set in and would love to see more games being made in this time period. It nails it perfectly all around.
-Graphics
- Graphics were great, they looked a ton better than i expected them to be. Lightyears better than the first game. And quite a lot better than other games from its time.
-Controls
- Controls felt fine on a controller, no complaints there. The keyboard/mouse controls could have used a bit of work. Example - getting rid of mouse acceleration would have been nice.
-Customization
- Love the fact that i can customize my car and even choose my clothes. Although i think it shuld have been more in depth than it was.
-Music
- Great music overall but i feel like there was a shortage of songs, i felt like i would re hear the same songs quite often and there was only 3 radio stations. Did they remove a lot of music to re release the game due to licensing?
-Cars/Driving
- Love the cars and the driving in this game. They all felt like they had real weight to them and all performed differently.
Cons
-Paper thin story
- Just like the first game, there was no real story here. I feel like i was doing missions for the sake of doing missions or because the boss said so etc. There was no character building or developement. Vito never really builds relationships with anyone. Most of the characters i have forgotten the names of with the exception of Joe. Overall i just felt like i was bouncing from random mission to random mission.
-Zero things to do in the city
- Maybe i missed something but just like in the first game there is nothing to do in the city. There is gas stations, places to eat/drink, mechanics, gun stores and clothing stores. Thats it. I would have loved it if i could go play pool or cards, perhaps go to a drive in theatre or anything other than doing missions. The city was so big and cool to see but it was completely void of things to do other than exploring for the sake of exploring.
-Collectibles used as a poor excuse to put something to do in the city
- So i saw there was Playboy mags and Wanted posters to find. Honestly i found a total of 3 Playboy mags and zero wanted posters. I hate collectibles in games in general but this just felt like it was filling a check box on the development paper.
-No free roam
- Would have loved some sort of basic free roaming without having to be in a mission all the time. Some missions you cant even begin to free roam as you have other characters with you or are thrown directly into the mission when you leave your appartment. And when you beat the game you cant even go free roaming then either! You have to make an entirely new game if you want to which really sucks as i planned on finally taking the time to explore the city in full.
Overall the game was fun to play and i am looking forward to Mafia 3, but it felt like a mission based game like Halo but built inside a large open city with nothing in it to do. Even still though, despite all the stuff i didnt like, i would still recommend it to everyone. I still had a blast just looking at everything and enjoying how beautiful the game was.
This is an epic game i reccomend it. and cant wait to play mafia 3

The Baconing is a RPG-ish and hack'n'slash-y adventure game with hilariously stupid and funny dialogues, revolving around the justice-loving hero DeathSpank.
In typical RPG-manner you acquire main- and side-quests as you fight your way through the varying and - thanks to the graphical art style of the game -really good looking areas of Spanktopia.
During the course of the game you constantly find new equipment in the form of weapons, armor, potions and gadgets to assist you in fighting hordes of mad turtles, dinosaurs, aliens, roboters and other enemies. The levelling system (up to level 20) also awards you with more health, damage or other perks upon reaching a new level.
The game can be played both alone and in local co-op (one player with keyboard and mouse, the other with a controller) and has a playtime of around 8-9 for a complete playthrough, probably a little less when playing in co-op.
Either way, I highly recommend The Baconing as it is great fun and well worth its money!

I bought this game back in 2014 and forgot about it until 2015 because it was not a finished product back when I bought it.  I tried to get as far as I could with it, but frustration and repetition set in.  The combat was nice at first, but it quickly became a chore to play.
Few spells gave decent damage for later levels and boss fights, and the game did not reward experimentation with spells.  If anything, it promotes sticking with the basic elements, fire, ice, and lightning.  All other spells become obsolete once you start making synergy spells because you can't combine any other triad of elements, and at badass difficulty, you're punished for swapping elements by having unequipped elements reset to level 1.  Whatever was the developer thinking when placing such limitations on spells when the entire game revolves around spell-making?
After a while, the novelty of the combat wears off, and you realize that spells don't really evolve over time.  You just shoot the same fireballs, the same lightning, the same ice shards from beginning to end with very little variance in either appearance or stats.  The lack of progress eventually made me too tired of the game to even finish the story mode.  I didn't even make it to the portals and Newb Game Plus.  I simply couldn't take the repetition and seemingly endless supply of enemies to kill.  I wanted more depth and more story; I wanted less running from point A to point B.

I picked up JUDGEMENT SILVERSWORD – Resurrection – up completely on a whim without knowing anything about the game.  I was looking for something to play and the low price point was enough to persuade me to give it a try.  There are a lot of bad to mediocre low-priced games out there that target impulse purchasers, and I'm happy to say that JUDGEMENT SILVERSWORD – Resurrection – does not fall into that category.
The two included games are somewhat obscure WonderSwan Color titles.  For anyone out there that doesn't know: the WonderSwan is a handheld game console that was released in Japan.  Judgement Silversword was the winner of a Bandai game development contest, and Cardinal Sins is a WonderSwan title based on Judgement Silversword but only playable through the WonderWitch Personal  Software Development Kit.  Physical copies of the game are quite rare, and very expensive, as it only received a limited commercial release in Japan.
Judgement Silversword is a more traditional shmup.  You fly through each stage destroying enemies and fighting bosses along the way.  It's a very challenging game, and unlike arcade style shooters you do not have infinite credits.  While playing the game and earning points you will unlock additional credits and other features.  The ship has two modes of fire and a shield which can also be used offensively.  The game will feel very familiar to individuals that have played the Judgement Silversword's spiritual successor ESCHATOS.
Cardinal Sins is a different type of game. Judging by the fact that this release was named JUDGEMENT SILVERSWORD – Resurrection –, I didn't really expect very much from the second game which isn't even referenced in the title.  Recycle edition isn't exactly a very flattering subtitle for a game either.  Despite its lack of prominent marketing, I ended up being more drawn into Cardinal Sins than I was Judgement Silversword.  It has seven different stages, each of which has a special objective. You are graded on each individual stage, and the game gives you an average letter grade at the end.  If the player performs well enough they will be rewarded with a chance to find the final boss.  Cardinal Sins is a short and fast paced game perfect for people that are in the mood to play a quick game during a lunch break or between other activities.  I've had a lot of fun trying to beat my personal best scores, and it is truly a shame that the Steam release doesn't have a global leader-board.
The graphical and audio aspects are about what one would expect from an older handheld release.  It looks and sounds fine, and fortunately has aged well.  It would have been nice to have more audio tracks but I suspect there aren't so many due to the technical limitations of the WonderSwan.  I enjoyed what was there, and even recognized one song that was later recreated in ESCHATOS.  The visuals are clear and bullets are easy to distinguish.  My only criticism in regards to graphics is of a very brief section of Cardinal Sins where the colors suddenly change.  It was slightly disorienting the first time I saw it, but a non-issue once I knew what to expect.
Overall JUDGEMENT SILVERSWORD – Resurrection – is a great package.  It offers two great shmups at a very low price.  I'm glad these were brought to Steam as they are WonderSwan titles I was completely unfamiliar with and most likely wouldn't have had the opportunity to play otherwise.  As previously mentioned, it's unfortunate that the game doesn't have leader-boards, but fortunately this isn't something that at all detracts from the gameplay.  I definitely recommend buying this, they're solid shooters and great bang for the buck.  If you're a fan of the genre you really can't go wrong with this one.
EDIT: October 6th, 2016 - It has leaderboards now!  Buy this game!

Judgement Silversword -Resurrection- is a vertical shmup in where your spaceship is as powerful as it is ever going to get from the very start. There are no power-ups and no bombs to clear the screen of bullets, just you and your skills is what can get you through this game. While the first dozen or so level may seem like a cake walk, things will quickly escalate from there and you will have so many projectiles shot at you that it nearly feels like it belongs in the Bullet Hell genre. The game features 30+ waves of enemies to get through and using one of your two continues will start you at the beginning of that wave. Using a continue usually means something went really badly for you as lives are rather plentiful and you will constantly see them drop. If the extra life item reaches the bottom of the screen then it will bounce back up for a short while but will be lost if it reaches the bottom of the screen again. It is a very real possibility to lose extra lifes to the abyss of space due to all the things on screen trying to kill you, so it is best to find an opening and retrieve it as soon as possible.
To defend yourself you will have a wide shot attack that fills the screen with your projectiles and works great against a swarm of weak enemies or if you are too focused avoiding bullets to use your narrow shot. Your narrow shot is exactly what it sounds like and shoots a condensed wave of projectiles at your foes that will quickly annihilate them though it is best used against the tougher enemies since it can be easier to get overwhelmed by numbers if you don't use it effectively. If things get too hectic and you have no means of escaping projectiles your spaceship also has a shield that can disintegrate certain projectiles and slow the others down. It is a small, front mounted shield however, so you are still vulnerable from the sides and the back. It does have an energy meter that quickly refills itself but you will likely never run out due having a ton. That doesn't mean you can just sit back and shake off the all the projectiles however, as that will more likely then not result in you being overwhelmed. This is the kind of game where you want to shoot the enemies as soon as they appear and are able to attack you. One bullet is all it takes to do you in so it leads to some rather intense moments of switching from offensive to defensive at a moments notice.
One thing that gave me a bad first impression was the ear-grating music that plays from wave 1-20. It is a song with a rather short loop and quickly grew annoying. The rest of the songs are fine and kind of catchy strangely enough, though most of your time will be spent hear that single tune. There is no story to speak of here, just you, your spaceship and tons of enemies to shoot down. There is a decent amount of enemy variety and they all have their own style of attacking. Some may try to crash into you, other will surround you by flying in a circle around you and one particularly nasty fellow will shoot unblock-able beams at you. None look visually memorable but it is still rather important to learn how they fight so you can be able to plan ahead and now what to expect. Bosses are rather hit or miss. Some are fun to fight like a sword carrying mech and others like a small unappealing cube are rather lame. They will all be the end of you if you don't focus on the fight and can take a heck of a lot of punishment. Barraging them with your narrow shot is far more effective than slowly damaging them with your spread shot though not suggested if you don't think you can navigate through all the projectiles. Some form of indication as to how damaged the boss is or a simple life bar would have been a nice addition as it can drag on a bit.
Another oversight of boss fights are that they are introduced via text on screen but that very same text can hide projectiles that are shot at you for the duration that it is there. The graphics of this game are pretty outdated and unappealing though they do the job. It is a port from a portable system called the “Wonderswan” and was released in 2004 to it's defense. In the options menu you can rotate the screen if you like to pivot your monitor for that arcade like experience and it does support HD resolutions like 2560x1440p nicely enough. Not many environments to look at I'm afraid. Most of your time will be spent in the blackness of space though you will see some planets from time to time and have an space battle on the moon. It is still the same game as Judgement Silversword however, it has the same music, enemies, bosses and everything else only that you now have objectives. After you complete all the 7 Sins you will be graded as to how well you did and go on to fight a boss. The way you go through areas have been remixed and the only other difference I could spot was that you now have less invincibility frames after respawning so get out of the way of projectiles if possible. All in all it did feel like a neat little side mode, not so much a two games in one package type of ordeal. Was not expecting much from Judgement Silversword -Resurrection- to be honest but to my surprise it turned out to be an addictive pleasure. It is a fast paced game that pulls no punches, even on easy mode you will need lots of skill to beat the game. I bought this game back in 2014 and forgot about it until 2015 because it was not a finished product back when I bought it.  I tried to get as far as I could with it, but frustration and repetition set in.  The combat was nice at first, but it quickly became a chore to play.
Few spells gave decent damage for later levels and boss fights, and the game did not reward experimentation with spells.  If anything, it promotes sticking with the basic elements, fire, ice, and lightning.  All other spells become obsolete once you start making synergy spells because you can't combine any other triad of elements, and at badass difficulty, you're punished for swapping elements by having unequipped elements reset to level 1.  Whatever was the developer thinking when placing such limitations on spells when the entire game revolves around spell-making?
After a while, the novelty of the combat wears off, and you realize that spells don't really evolve over time.  You just shoot the same fireballs, the same lightning, the same ice shards from beginning to end with very little variance in either appearance or stats.  The lack of progress eventually made me too tired of the game to even finish the story mode.  I didn't even make it to the portals and Newb Game Plus.  I simply couldn't take the repetition and seemingly endless supply of enemies to kill.  I wanted more depth and more story; I wanted less running from point A to point B.

Stronghold series has been in deep trouble and continues to do so. That is very sad thing, because I really liked the original stronghold games. Buy either original Stronghold or Stronghold Crusader or wait and hope that the Stronghold Crusader 2 will be better.
Full review:
The developers of Stronghold 3 said that they attempted to return back to the roots of original Stronghold games after that Stronghold 2 and Stronghold Legends had been disappointments. Personally I don't see that much resemblance between original Stronghold games and Stronghold 3. This might not have been the problem, because this series might require refreshing instead of going back to roots. Whatever the developers tried to do, the game is a failure. This result was heavily affected by the fact that the publisher pushed the game to markets before it was ready. Now the game doesn't have any game braking bugs anymore but some annoying bugs still exist and the gameplay just isn't nearly as good as it should be.
I'll start with the gameplay. The gamplay is too slow. The gameplay in the actual Stronghold games has always been slower than in the Crusader versions to place more value on the economy but in this game the gameplay is just too slow. The units are too slow and also the economy is also extremely slow. Even new citizens spawn too slowly. The result of this is that the army sizes are extremely low as well as the size of the castle.
Next i'll talk more specifically about the economy. The economy in this game seems to be very difficult to manage. It seems like that no matter the player does, the player is all the time on the edge of collapse of the economy even if the enemies don't attack you castle. Even worse is how popularity is calculated. Before this game the popularity was very stable once the most basic needs of the citisens were secured. In Stronghold Crusader 3 however the popularity changes all the time because
a) the economy is all the time on the edge of collapse
b) amount of population has drastic effect on popularity
c) Popularity is always going up or down unlike in previous game in which it was easy to have stable popularity.
The result of both economy and popularity being at the edge of collapse is that the player uses almost all the time micromanaging these things leaving no time to build the defenses or care about the army in a game in which half of the game should be doing these two things.
Third main problem in this game is the castle building. The building of walls and towers was changed dramatically for this game, but unfortunately the new system is total disaster. It is difficult to use and some of the difficulty might actually be caused by bugs. In a game, where economy is requiring your constant micromanaging and enemies attack every now and then a difficult to use waal bulding system is huge problem. The new system also prevents the creation of imaginative castles. On top of this the player is unable to create moats around his castle inexcept in the scenario builder. The developers have admitted their mistake and the building of walls and towers will be reverted to how it was before for Stronghold Crusader 2.
Fourth main problem is the combat. The combat is very slow and units under melee attack are very unresponsive. This makes makes usage of fast troops pointless. In previous games I preferred to have mixed army (because different units had their own strenghts), but in this game only useful troops are swordmen and crossbowmen. Exception being knights that are needed to destroy siege engines.
To summarise the gameplay part: Stronghold crusader is a game combining medieval combat, castle building and economy and it fails in all these aspects.
Last thing that I would like to mention are graphics. The graphics of this game are awful. Both the soldiers and buildings are are very difficult to distinguish from each other and I also dislike the chosen artistic style. If the developers of this game can't create clear and beutiful 3D objects they should revert back to 2.5D graphics that was used in original stronhold game because that game had very beautiful and clear graphics.

I have mixed feelings about this game. Its creative and easy to pick up and play, with decision based events that make it feel like you really have a say in how things work out for you in the long run. Its a great game with a solid feel to it, and it's very addictive to keep trying with new ships and crew members.
My real problem with it is the luck factor it seems to have. Sometimes you can be floating around and find scrap (currency), new weapons, or random new teammates to join you. But the other half of the time its less than "fun" events that get dealt to you for no real reason. You could decide a very cautious run and choose to not interact with any distractions that come your way, and still find yourself in a situation where your ship catches fire as a battle starts, or inside a nebula which deactivate all your shields or weapons, or just up against a random encounter enemy that can wipe your ship because its ridiculously overpowered. You could make the best decisions, have a fully upgraded ship with crazy firepower and shields, with a reliable crew, and still get tripped up in a random event that causes something to go downhill simply because the game feels like it. But that's not what really upsets me, I could deal with that stuff if it wasn't for the final boss.
The final boss is extremely aggravating, literally one of the worst difficulty spikes in a game i've ever seen. It's a three stage fight against one mega ship that varies its attacks based on which form it's in. After you defeat one of its forms it fully heals itself with no real explanation or signs of getting weaker, as would be assumed of a ship or enemy that you literally blow apart with each encounter, meanwhile your ship doesn't get to be repaired at all. The final form is a super shielded version of the previous two with a "secret weapon" that just HAPPENS to be implemented in its last fight. This "secret weapon" launches a barrage of lasers which instantly wipe your shields and damage you no matter what. This barrage is used while the boss' other weapons are still in use, and it is activated quite frequently during this fight. This is not how you establish a boss fight, this is a cheap and boring way to make your game seem difficult. Even with a fully upgraded ship with four shields and over 50% evasion I was wiped out without much of a chance. Im not expecting to jump into the fight and crush the boss without any opposition. This fight should be enjoyable and challenging, rather than some ridiculously overpowered means to halt your well deserved conclusion.
I think this is a well made game with some well deserved positive reviews and opinions. The music is captivating and enhances the atmosphere amazingly. The variety in gameplay is more than enough to keep you coming back to try the many ships, crew, weapons, and all kinds of combinations it offers. The game is pleasant to look at and gives you a simple layout that doesn't try to complicate things or clutters the screen with text, and isn't intimidating to pick up and try out.
But the only thing that forces me to not recommend this game, despite it's genuine potential to be great, really is that final boss and luck factor. If the constant loss from running into a negative situation isn't enough to discourage players, then the final boss constantly crushing you will. I honestly can't count the number of times I made it to that last stage only to be severely punished for trying to earn the ending despite my best efforts time and time again. This game is half skill and half luck. I really wish it wasn't though.

While basic, Judgement Silversword is a decent, well-ported little shmup. Interesting enemies and bullet patterns, but scoring is pretty lacking. These are great games.  Do not be mistaken by my assassment of this particular port. This review speaks to the product at the state that it was originally relased on Steam. The games herein still play like butter and are highly refined examples of why the shmup/shooter/STG genre is so compelling, fun, and relevent.
However, one of the key componets for games like these is Score chasing.  These two games are built around the idea of "high-score".  All of the gameplay mechanics within are in service to the scoring system itself.  If one can agree with this, then one may find the lack of online Leaderboards in this Steam version to be a very huge disappointment.  Online leaderboards shouldn't be an afterthought or a missing feature for modern games of this type.
What makes this even more frustrating is that I own these games in their previous incarnation on the Xbox 360.  That version, which is what I beleve this port was ported from, has fully funtional online leaderboards.  That version remains the superior version, play it there if you don't wanna feel like you've been cut-off from the rest of the world.
So close to being pure bliss it hurts.

In episode 135 of Bullet Heaven HD, we FINALLY take a look at Judgement Silversword and Cardinal Sins, newly released to Steam on September 18, 2015. These games make up over a grand in software and hardware to play in their original state; so what's the fuss all about? Let's take a look!

A vast amount of my playtime from this comes from the Xbox 360 version of Eschatos, however this is an absolutely excellent port with just a single problem - Lack of online leaderboards.
The Xbox 360 versions of these ports had online leaderboards and that's a pretty weird oversight for this release, especially considering Eschatos has them in place! With that said though, it's a set of two absolutely exceptional shmups that no fan of the genre should go without playing. Graphically simple but incredibly involving.
Judgement Silversword was a Wonderwitch title that won a development competition and got a cartridge release for the Bandai Wonderswan. It's an excellent shmup with great scoring that's just damn fun to play.
Cardinal Sins is more of a 'skill test' type of game, with objective based stages named after the 7 deadly sins. For example, envy has you destroying everything, and your score is based on destruction rate. Wrath has you vs. a boss throwing a screen full of bullets at you, and your score is based on how many times you've died.
The grades you get throughout these 7 stages determine what bonuses you get for the final boss fight, which is extremely difficult.
The two games bundled are amazing examples of good shmup mechanics and I'd highly recommend to any shmup fan. At this price it feels like I'm stealing.

I have mixed feelings about this game. Its creative and easy to pick up and play, with decision based events that make it feel like you really have a say in how things work out for you in the long run. Its a great game with a solid feel to it, and it's very addictive to keep trying with new ships and crew members.
My real problem with it is the luck factor it seems to have. Sometimes you can be floating around and find scrap (currency), new weapons, or random new teammates to join you. But the other half of the time its less than "fun" events that get dealt to you for no real reason. You could decide a very cautious run and choose to not interact with any distractions that come your way, and still find yourself in a situation where your ship catches fire as a battle starts, or inside a nebula which deactivate all your shields or weapons, or just up against a random encounter enemy that can wipe your ship because its ridiculously overpowered. You could make the best decisions, have a fully upgraded ship with crazy firepower and shields, with a reliable crew, and still get tripped up in a random event that causes something to go downhill simply because the game feels like it. But that's not what really upsets me, I could deal with that stuff if it wasn't for the final boss.
The final boss is extremely aggravating, literally one of the worst difficulty spikes in a game i've ever seen. It's a three stage fight against one mega ship that varies its attacks based on which form it's in. After you defeat one of its forms it fully heals itself with no real explanation or signs of getting weaker, as would be assumed of a ship or enemy that you literally blow apart with each encounter, meanwhile your ship doesn't get to be repaired at all. The final form is a super shielded version of the previous two with a "secret weapon" that just HAPPENS to be implemented in its last fight. This "secret weapon" launches a barrage of lasers which instantly wipe your shields and damage you no matter what. This barrage is used while the boss' other weapons are still in use, and it is activated quite frequently during this fight. This is not how you establish a boss fight, this is a cheap and boring way to make your game seem difficult. Even with a fully upgraded ship with four shields and over 50% evasion I was wiped out without much of a chance. Im not expecting to jump into the fight and crush the boss without any opposition. This fight should be enjoyable and challenging, rather than some ridiculously overpowered means to halt your well deserved conclusion.
I think this is a well made game with some well deserved positive reviews and opinions. The music is captivating and enhances the atmosphere amazingly. The variety in gameplay is more than enough to keep you coming back to try the many ships, crew, weapons, and all kinds of combinations it offers. The game is pleasant to look at and gives you a simple layout that doesn't try to complicate things or clutters the screen with text, and isn't intimidating to pick up and try out.
But the only thing that forces me to not recommend this game, despite it's genuine potential to be great, really is that final boss and luck factor. If the constant loss from running into a negative situation isn't enough to discourage players, then the final boss constantly crushing you will. I honestly can't count the number of times I made it to that last stage only to be severely punished for trying to earn the ending despite my best efforts time and time again. This game is half skill and half luck. I really wish it wasn't though.
