At the moment, I think this is the cutoff point of the series being good. You’ll hear people saying the older games are better than these newer ones, but I think this game looks good and still has that classic Worms vibe that the older ones had without any additional gimmicks. If you like Worms and want to play it with friends, this is the one I would pick up if you aren’t too fussed about “classic Worms purity.”
For those that don’t know about Worms, essentially you and your opponents are put on a (usually big) map with four Worms each, and every player takes a turn to make a move while the game swaps through each of your worms each of your turns. Movement is rather limited, with worms moving very slow and jumping rather low while on a turn timer. While there are limited items that alleviate this like the jetpack, most of the gameplay is about aiming your weapons properly around the environment with wind affecting it. And this game has a LOT of different weapons. From standard grenades to chuck and rocket launchers to fire…to air strikes, earthquakes, baseball bats, and exploding grandmothers, this game certainly has a lot of variety. The catch is that you only have a limited amount to start with and need to get more through air drops that land wherever on the map. It’s certainly fun chaos with friends as you not only try to knock other people out, but also try to keep yourself alive…either with positioning of your worms or trying to form alliances to get your friend to aim at another instead. There’s a reason this series is so well-known, after all!

This is my favourite game of all time, the aesthetic, monsters/bosses, plot, environments, characters, are all unique and can't be compared to any other Final Fantasy experience I've had. For me, this has always been the best Final Fantasy game. I've played it over and over and enjoyed it fully every time, it's a timeless classic.

+ The gameplay is great, especially if you are a fan of tradional turn-based RPGs. They are however "Active Time Battles" which means the battle does not stop while selecting your attack.
+ Visually the game has a great style. I would call it "Chibi" as all the characters look short and cute, and intended to be not as serious as other final fantasy games.  Just like FFVII a lot of the backgrounds are still images while the characters are 3D. I thought it typically looked great, but occasionally it was hard to tell what I was looking at. (keep in mind this game was made on the Playstation 1 back in 2000)
+ Overall has a great story. In the beginning it kinda played out like a Disney movie. You are kidnapping a Princess, but you find out the Princess actually wanted to escape and explore the world, and it turns into a bit of a love story of a Princess and a lowly thief named Zidane. Personally, I'd highly recommend this game to people who enjoy more lighthearted stories that make you smile as there's quite a lot of comedy thrown in as well.  The story does however get pretty dark and tragic later on, but I don't want to spoil it.
+ The monsters you fight are very diverse and all very interesting.
+ Lots of bosses (especially at the end of the game) who are all challenging, and an absolute joy to defeat.
+ Epic ending. Not to spoil it too much, but you fight like 10 bosses one after another, and they are all amazing
+ You learn abilities from the equipment you find. Once you learn the ability you can give the equipment to someone else and have them learn from the piece. I found this to be really neat. Unfortunetely, a lot of the equipment (especially weapons) are locked to specific characters which limits the freedom to create your own classes.
+ Synthesis shops which let you combine multiple items to create new more powerful gear. Honestly, this is something every RPGs should have as it makes every item have a purpose.
+ For the PC release, there's addional features like the "speed up time" button F1 which makes grinding for levels/experience SO MUCH easier, and also helps reduce long animations like auto-potion or Eidolen summons.
+ The Eidolens or Summoning creatures all have great attack animations, and are really neat looking creatures.
+ Some of the characters have great personalities, especially Eiko
+ Fantastic soundtrack
+ ~35-40hours of content that never felt repetitive
~ There is a TON of cutscenes in this game with an overload of dialogue. To some this may be great, to others this may be tiresome as it involves a lot of reading and a lot of non-essential character development scenes.
- A few story / character elements did not make a lot of sense, and left a very poor mark on the story overall. For instance, Queen Brahne of Alexandria seems to randomly turn evil and suddenly (without any reason) tries to take over the world. This is never explained as to what her motive is, and it's a main plot point...
- The battle system unfortunetely has some issues. When you select an attack it does not go off right away. It's basically "queued" and you have to wait a considerable amount of time for the character to actually attack based on their speed. This can be problematic as the enemy could say poison a character (which inflicts damage every few seconds real time) and since your party of already queued up you can't stop to use a potion.
- Just a personal note, but I did not like some of the main characters and some had no real part in the story at all. Steiner the Knight is incredibly annoying always accusing everyone of being criminals (sort of like having a police officer follow you around everywhere). Quina just wants food all the time serving no real purpose story wise. Amarant joins the party later, but acts like he doesn't want to be a part of anything and also serves no purpose story wise.
- Throughout almost the entire game you can not see enemy health bars, and do not know when they will die.
- Eating monsters to learn abilities for Quina is painstakingly annoying. You must drop a creatures hp down to below 25%. Like previously mentioned, you do not know how much health enemies have.
- "Trance" the overdrive system is hardly ever used throughout the game, and some characters "trance" without having special moves which is disappointing.
- There are a lot of infuriating status ailments like confuse, berserk, sleep, freeze, death, stop, gradual petrify,  petrify, and so fourth that either kill the character, make you lose control of the character (so they end up attacking themselves or your own party), or get frozen in place unable to move. There's also other status ailments like Zombie and Virus when prevent your character from earning experience or AP points....
- The Thieving system absolutely sucks in FFIX. Basically every boss has ~3 items you can steal. First item has a 100% chance to steal, second item has 25% chance, and 3rd item (which is the item you want) has a ~0.5% - 6% chance to steal (ridiculously low). Zidane is the only one who knows Steal, so basically...instead of trying to defeat a boss you are waiting around stealing for god knows how long and hoping you get lucky. It's beyond stupid.
[Side Note] Like most final fantasy games you really need to play the game from start to finish to truly experience the game. Just keep that in mind if you decide to pick this up as if you just play the beginning you might not enjoy it as much.

EDIT:  This review was my first time playing this game(or any FF).
This is quite possibly THE best game I've ever played in my life, as well as(technically) the first and only Final Fantasy I've ever played. I'm not too knowledgable on the "Final Fantasy politics" but what I do know is that this game is, still to this day, known as one of the best Final Fantasy games ever and boy are there a lot of reasons to love this game beyond "just to kill time". Do note that, like all reviews, this is my opinion and facts mixed e.g. discuss the gameplay, give my opinion. So, let's get on with this review, goof ball!
The story is, to put it bluntly, ♥♥♥♥ing AMAZING. From the screenshots, you should immedietally get a medieval-fantasy vibe to it, and you're not wrong at all. That's basically what 90% of the game is. Similar to previous FF games, it also has eidolon / summoner magic, and steam-themed stuff, such as airships(specifically this, to be honest). The story, for the most part, focuses on two main characters(emotional romance relationship rather than physical), one sub-main character, and the rest being side characters / not as important as the others. The story's overall point also doesn't boil down to "bad guy is bad, must save world". It has some legitimate morals and ideas in the story, regardless of whethernot you've heard them before. An example is a character who feels "out of place" because of who they are, but finds strength in the friends they are with as a reason to continue living.
It took me about 50~ hours, with the fast-forwarding feature(will explain this later) to bypass grinding and monotony in the minigame(s), while not getting *everything*, but most of it. So, if you don't use the fast-forwarding feature, I'd say about 60-70 hours of a single playthrough. That's pretty lengthy for a $23.99 game and guess what? The pacing of the game? I'd say it was nearly perfect(nothing is ever perfect), so much so that I never felt bored or annoyed at any point of the game. It all flowed very nicely. In reality, there is a lot I can't(won't) say about the story itself without spoiling anything, so unfortunately you have to experience it yourself. The FF series is a series of quality and experience. All I can personally say is it involves eidolons(basically summoning titan-like creatures, such as the Leviathan, Bahamut(King of Dragons), and an Ifrit(fire spirit)) and a lot of bad stuff happening. The ending is
. It's worth it to sit through the credits and just get this big wave of amazement thrown at you. It was a great feel and it's probably going to stick around for a while.
The gameplay is your standard JRPG - turnbased. There's two combat options. Active, and Wait. Active means that the battle is in real-time(the action bar that fills up, when full a person's turn is then ready to be queued)
, so be careful when choosing that. I had some annoying moments because of it. Wait, on the other hand, pauses time when you open up a menu e.g. Attack menu, item menu, etc. I personally prefer Active as it puts you on edge, especially with many of the bosses, given that you don't over-grind earlier on like me. The "Limit Break" or "Powered Up" system in this game is built up by being hurt and the gained abilities last about 3~ turns with varying abilities depending on the character. Mages get 2 spell casts per turn, and the rest get improved versions of an ability or "limit break" abilities.
The minigames are pretty straight forward. There's a digging minigame with a chocobo, a 99% irrelevant and entirely-for-fun card minigame, an auction house, a frog-catching minigame, an annoying skip-rope minigame, and a very tiring race minigame. Only 3 of those are required to get beneficial items(with exception of the auction house which lets you get certain items earlier than usual, if you can afford it). Hint : It doesn't include the last two, so skip them if you become frustrated, it's not worth it. At all.
The graphics are PS1-era graphics but sort-of-kind-of improved slightly. They don't look a whole lot different from the PS1 version's graphics but the backgrounds... Now that's where people were annoyed when this game was originally ported. From what I recall, the backgrounds, at the very least besides everything else, weren't able to be recovered. So, essentially what they did was take picture of the backgrounds and use those. That's why they have a pastel-esque look to them on some(most in my opinion) of the backgrounds. Now all of that out of the way, I think what is specifically amazing is the animation cinematics. They easily still hold up today and they look AMAZING. There are a few moments in the game where they have the in-game character model with the animated cinematics playing around it, and it looks amazing, but the cinematics themselves are just fascinatingly beautiful to look at, and they still hold up today.
I feel like JRPGs(asian-made games in general, I guess?) specifically put in the time and effort to focus on the music because music adds to context, provides atmosphere, and overall just sets the mood/emotion of anything. It's never a bad thing to have music alongside a narrative. Is the music good in this game? Yes, it's amazing, just like my terrible ability to create suspense in my overall point. The battle music and fanfare fit together nicely, and the different music used for different types of scenes (e.g. heartfelt scenes never had unfitting music) and, best of all, the boss music for specific battles was amazing, specifically the pivotal villain's theme/boss music. I loved it. Overall, the music was great. Think how Chrono Cross did it music, and you'll get the idea. Everything fit perfectly. The music was like the cherry-on-top of the amazing game-cake, ESPECIALLY the credits music, again similar to Chrono Cross in how amazing it was.
Other stuff that I'm not confidently able to fit into anywhere else
Synthesis is basically an item-creation system in which you synthesise(combine) two items to create one. Chemistry, everyone! Except with solid objects, and not necessarily with chemicals.
Lots of secrets(Example being two secret bosses that I found, but there's a couple more I think, depending on whether not you do everything in the game, e.g. a side-quest at the end of the game).
Achievements, which is a nice addition.
You DO NOT need to be max level to beat the game. I beat it with a level 60~ party, and beat the secret optional boss at around the same level. Most of the game is about tactics / knowing how to deal with status effects, certain abilities, etc.
There are certain features(7 "Game Boosters") that were added to this port, that mainly serve to allow you to enjoy the story and not worry about grinding, difficulty, etc. I'm going to speed-fire them.
Toggle on / off : 9999 damage, fast forward(double speed(I think, possibly more) but doesn't affect the in-game's clock, which means timed sequences are unaffected), full Trance(limit break), no encounters.
Permanent on save : master all skills upon equipping respective item, max ability stones & level, max GIL.
If you find a golden toad and don't have the achievement yet, save then catch it, and reload. It is very much a benefit to having it in a swamp and there's no actual benefit to catching it. The benefit also only applies to the current swamp it resides in, the mentioned benefit being faster frog respawn/growth rates.
Feedback on the review would be nice. I like writing reviews and I'm trying to finding more games I'm passionate about. This game was amazing and all of this came from the heart/mind/etc. Tried to be genuine in what I thought about the game. Let's get the ugly bits out of the way. This game did not work when I first downloaded it (Linux). I had to reboot a couple times, use the update tool, and then suddenly - success, I got the game to launch! I'm pretty sure the default video mode was unhappy with my dual-monitor setup. This is standard fare for Linux gaming, so I was not dissuaded.
Once I had it running, I was very impressed. This game is clearly in beta; there are occasional graphical glitches and inline error codes that really don't impact gameplay at all. Looking beyond this, however, we see a highly immersive and surprisingly well-polished MMO. There are several interesting and unique features that make this game stand out, even when stacked against its more well-funded peers. The regular PvE game is nicely paced and the quests are for the most part easy to follow. From what I've seen, the classes are well-balanced and there are enough features to keep things interesting for a very long time. The postgame feature, 3-way RvR, is a really great idea and stands out in the crowd. I'm not much of a PvP guy, but this system really makes me want try it and stick with it. As it stands now, the game is great, and I love playing it - but the potential for greatness is immense.
